Signal Processing.summary: Non-invasive brain-to-text interfaces offer alternative communication pathways for people with communication disabilities. However, sentence-level decoding from electroencephalography (EEG) remains challenging. We propose a hierarchical EEG-text alignment framework that retrieves previously unseen sentences by progressively decoding coarse-grained semantic information and fine-grained sentence representations. We hypothesize that broader semantic context can be more reliably captured from EEG than individual sentences. Accordingly, EEG representations are first classified into semantic classes, which are defined as groups of related sentences, followed by sentence retrieval within the predicted class. Among over 2,000 unique text samples, our approach achieves, on unseen sentences, average top-5 and top-10 retrieval accuracies of 62.6\% $\pm$ 1.0\% and 83.5\% $\pm$ 1.0\%, respectively, compared with 0.3\% $\pm$ 0.3\% and 0.5\% $\pm$ 0.2\% for direct EEG-sentence alignment without semantic classification. Qualitative analysis further reveals that decoding performance depends strongly on textual context. These findings demonstrate the potential of hierarchical semantic alignment for advancing sentence-level EEG-to-text decoding.

Signal Processing.title: QoS-Constrained Sum-Rate Maximization in RIS-Assisted Pinching-Antenna NOMA Systems
Signal Processing.summary: This paper investigates a two-user downlink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) system jointly assisted by a single-waveguide pinching-antenna system (PASS) and a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). To maximize the achievable sum rate under quality-of-service (QoS) constraints, the pinching antenna (PA) positions, RIS phase shifts, and power allocation coefficients are jointly optimized. The resulting non-convex optimization problem is addressed using an alternating optimization (AO) framework, where power allocation is obtained in closed form, while RIS phase shifts and PA positions are optimized through majorization-minimization (MM) and sequential quadratic programming (SQP), respectively. Numerical results show that the proposed architecture achieves higher sum rates than conventional-antenna and PASS-only benchmarks. Moreover, the MM- and SQP-based optimization stages achieve performance comparable to semidefinite relaxation (SDR) and grid-based exhaustive search, respectively, while the AO algorithm exhibits rapid convergence.

Signal Processing.title: Embodied Intelligence for Spectrum Map Construction in Low-Altitude Wireless Networks
Signal Processing.summary: Accurate spectrum map construction by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is crucial for intelligent resource management in low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs). Although various construction approaches have been investigated, their performance often degrades under extremely sparse sampling because purely data-driven models may not capture the underlying propagation physics. To address these challenges, an embodied intelligence framework is proposed, which synergistically integrates closed-loop perception-cognition-execution (PCE) coupling and embodied exploration to achieve precise and efficient spectrum construction. Based on this framework, a corresponding embodied cognition and decision network (ECDNet) with three tightly coupled modules is designed. Specifically, by leveraging distance-aware convolutions, the semantic bridge, and adaptive feature alignment mechanisms, ECDNet establishes the bidirectional information flow between construction and decision-making. Simulation results show that ECDNet achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) of 2.787 dBm at 4.00% sampling under the non-revisiting spiral protocol. Furthermore, a practical UAV-based spectrum construction platform is developed and field-deployed to provide prototype-level evidence that the sensing, cognition, and action modules execute as a closed loop on size, weight, and power constrained UAV edge devices.
Signal Processing.comment: 14 pages, 9 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing

Signal Processing.title: How to Receive Focused Beams in Near-Field MIMO? Analytical Combiners and Array Size Optimization
Signal Processing.summary: This paper investigates receive combining for near-field beamfocusing in line-of-sight channels with antenna array misalignment. We propose and evaluate two analytical combiners: analog ANF-AC and digital ANF-DC. Beyond focusing the beam toward the transmitter, ANF-AC benefits from the proposed phase-flip corrections (PFCs), while ANF-DC additionally exploits Dirichlet-kernel-based amplitude tapering. ANF-AC closely matches theoretically optimal analog equal-gain combining (EGC), with an SNR gap below 0.006 dB. Similarly, ANF-DC matches optimal digital maximum-ratio combining (MRC). We then leverage the analytical properties of these combiners for link-level evaluation and optimization, deriving a closed-form expression for the optimal transmitter-receiver array-size trade-off that maximizes received SNR with analog combining. We also show that the optimized analog receiver performs within 0.84 dB of its fully digital MRC-equivalent counterpart. These results demonstrate that optimized analog combining (with potentially lower implementation complexity and cost, particularly at higher frequencies) can get close to the fully digital performance. Beyond the theoretical insights presented, the analytical tractability and EGC-like / MRC-like performance of our combiners enable accurate network-level mathematical studies of beamfocusing, such as coverage, capacity, and interference analysis and optimization toward efficient 6G+ near-field MIMO communication systems.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, Submitted to IEEE ICC 2027

Signal Processing.title: Low-Power Spiking Neural Network Acceleration with Differential Time Representation: A Modular Hardware Framework
Signal Processing.summary: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer promising energy efficiency, making them well suited for energy-constrained applications. Much of their energy savings stems from the sparse encoding of spike trains. We show that spike trains can be represented more efficiently using Differential Time Representation (DTR), which requires fewer bits than Address-Event Representation (AER) or equidistantly sampled 1-bit spike trains. To support multiple input spike trains, we provide a rigorous proof that DTR sequences can be merged with low complexity. We also provide a set of modular hardware streaming components using this representation that can be flexibly connected to construct custom accelerator architectures for specific SNNs. Tailoring the hardware architecture to the selected SNN is streamlined by a Python framework combining the modular hardware components into a full SNN implementation. We use the framework to generate three accelerators for the Spiking Heidelberg Digits (SHD), Spiking Speech Commands (SSC), and PSMNIST benchmarks, each in a throughput-optimized parallel variant and a resource-reduced time-multiplexed variant. We report results for FPGA and ASIC implementations, the latter synthesized with a fully open-source flow targeting the predictive ASAP7 PDK. On the SHD dataset, the ASIC implementation reaches 92.46% classification accuracy, while sustaining $\approx{}$12,027 inferences per second at 20.37$μ$J per inference, exceeding the neuromorphic Loihi processor by 109$\times$ in throughput and 1.8$\times$ in energy efficiency. The corresponding FPGA implementation achieves $\approx{}$6,023 inferences per second without using DSP blocks. Across all three datasets, the synthesized ASICs reduce energy per inference by 27-37$\times$ relative to their FPGA counterparts, demonstrating that competitive SNN accelerators can be realized entirely within an open-source design flow.

Signal Processing.title: Robust inverse dielectric design of skin phantoms for implantable wireless link evaluation
Signal Processing.summary: Skin phantoms support reproducible evaluation of implantable wireless links, yet published complex permittivities of skin predict different propagation losses. We formulate a robust inverse design to determine a homogeneous phantom permittivity that minimizes the largest channel-loss difference across selected skin reference models, incidence angles and both transverse-electric and transverse-magnetic polarizations. Computed candidates and analytical lower bounds bracket the optimal mismatch and constrain the critical depth. Across seven frequencies from 5 to 500 GHz, the minimax mismatch at 1.3 mm ranges from 1.13 to 13.72 dB. For a 3 dB tolerance, suitable permittivities exist at every investigated depth at 5 GHz, while critical depths at the other frequencies range from 0.23 to 1.01 mm. Only one of seven material cases from the literature meets a 6 dB tolerance at 1.3 mm. These results translate channel-loss tolerances into quantitative design criteria for skin phantoms used in implantable wireless link evaluation.

Signal Processing.title: A Hybrid Analytical-Neural Residual Surrogate for Fast Radio Propagation Prediction over Irregular Terrain
Signal Processing.summary: Fast prediction of radio-wave propagation over irregular terrain is important for coverage analysis in mountainous environments, where many terrain and antenna configurations must be evaluated repeatedly. High-fidelity split-step parabolic equation (SSPE) solvers can capture terrain-induced shadowing and interference, but their computational cost is high for repeated planning studies. Learning-based surrogates reduce this cost, but direct field regression asks the network to learn both analytically tractable propagation trends and terrain-dependent residual structure. This paper proposes a hybrid analytical-neural residual surrogate that separates these two parts. A deterministic analytical baseline represents free-space spreading, antenna directivity, modified knife-edge diffraction, and terrain-aware specular reflection, while a compact coarse-to-fine neural network predicts the residual field. The network uses baseline-derived guidance channels, anisotropic convolutions, and feature-wise antenna conditioning to match the directional structure of terrain propagation fields. On synthetic SSPE data at 1.0 GHz, the proposed model achieves an MAE of 2.1061 dB, compared with 3.3955 dB for a standard U-Net and 3.2560 dB for a reproduced physics-guided CNN, while reducing the average inference time to 11.30 ms per sample. A zero-shot test at 1.8 GHz gives an MAE of 2.8692 dB without retraining, and a case study on the measured Hjorringvej terrain profile shows that the prediction remains consistent with the SSPE reference and follows the measured path-loss trend.
Signal Processing.comment: Under review at IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation

Signal Processing.title: Learning Regularization Structure for Biosignal Template Estimation
Signal Processing.summary: Objective: To estimate event-related templates of biosignals accurately from a small number of events. Methods: We design a template estimation algorithm that minimizes Stein's unbiased risk estimate (SURE) over a convolution kernel defining a Tikhonov penalty, learning its structure and magnitude from the data, and extend SURE to temporally correlated noise. We compare the resulting estimator, SURE(kernel), with established estimators in simulations and on auditory EEG, P300 (ten subjects), and ECG recordings. Results: In simulations, SURE(kernel) was the most accurate method at moderate and high noise levels and, at moderate noise, for every number of events tested; at low noise, generalized cross-validation was the most accurate. On real data with five events per class, SURE(kernel) was the closest of the compared estimators to the full-data references on the auditory EEG and in all ten P300 subjects. On ECG, averaging was closest; SURE(kernel) stayed within 3% of it, whereas generalized cross-validation and Empirical Bayes were 38% and 40% farther. On P300, SURE(kernel)'s template-implied event probabilities were less overconfident than those of averaging, at similar detection performance. On both EEG datasets, absolute accuracy at five events remained limited. Conclusion: Learning the regularization structure from the data, with a correction for correlated noise, can make templates estimated from few events more accurate than those of established estimators. Significance: The method yields more accurate templates when few events can be recorded, as in personalization or when collecting data from each user is costly, with better-calibrated event probabilities at similar detection performance.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering. 11 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables; supplementary material appended (14 pages)

Signal Processing.title: Multiple-Input Multiple-Output Forward Scatter Radar
Signal Processing.summary: Forward Scatter Radar (FSR) enhances the detection of low-observable targets by exploiting the increased radar cross section that occurs when a target crosses the transmitter-receiver baseline. Conventional FSR typically uses single-input single-output (SISO) architectures with limited localization capability, while recent single-input multiple-output (SIMO) systems enable non-coherent angular estimation. This paper introduces a multiple-input multiple-output FSR (MIMO-FSR) framework for joint estimation of target direction of departure (DoD) and direction of arrival (DoA) from non-coherent, amplitude-only measurements. By exploiting antenna arrays at both the transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX), the proposed approach enables two-dimensional angular localization without phase synchronization among TX/RX array elements. We establish the underlying operating principle under ideal signal separability and then develop practical frequency-division multiplexing (FDM) and time-division multiplexing (TDM) implementations. For each scheme, dedicated signal models and processing methods compensate for distortions caused by frequency offsets and target motion, respectively. We also derive analytical expressions for angular resolution, ambiguity conditions, and output-map distortions. Extensive numerical simulations for short- and long-baseline scenarios reveal operational limits and trade-offs between the two multiplexing schemes. Finally, proof-of-concept outdoor experiments using software-defined radio platforms validate the proposed framework. The results demonstrate joint DoD-DoA estimation and support the feasibility of MIMO-FSR for future active, passive, and integrated sensing and communications applications.

Signal Processing.title: Waveform Randomization for Secure ISAC Against Informed Eavesdroppers
Signal Processing.summary: We study waveform-level protection of Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) against a UAV-mounted eavesdropper (Eve) that knows the waveform construction and the phase-key generation rules. The novelty of this work is a systematic, budget-explicit attack analysis: instead of relying on undisclosed design details, we quantify what an informed Eve can learn and reconstruct, and how much computation this takes. We protect the sensing reference with Fourier-curve modulation, phase keys, and tangent Artificial Noise (AN), with burst- specific information shared over secure backhaul. We compare three key-generation rules against offline Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based sequence identification and online Adam and phase-aware expectation-maximization (EM) key recovery, under complete or partial nominal-sequence knowledge. A power- domain model couples residual key error with imperfect AN removal and predicts coherent delay locking. Results show that reusable key structure permits sequence identification even when demodulation fails, position-dependent keying raises recovery difficulty, and seed-expanded keying resists the evaluated clas- sifier within the learning budget. Waveform simulations under multipath, clutter, and echo accumulation confirm the sensing impact.
Signal Processing.comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Communication

Signal Processing.title: Robustness Evaluation of Machine Learning Models for Fault Classification and Localization In Power System Protection
Signal Processing.summary: The growing penetration of renewable and distributed generation is transforming power systems and challenging conventional protection schemes that rely on fixed settings and local measurements. Machine learning (ML) offers a data-driven alternative for centralized fault classification (FC) and fault localization (FL), enabling faster and more adaptive decision-making. However, practical deployment critically depends on robustness. Protection algorithms must remain reliable even when confronted with missing, noisy, or degraded sensor data. This work introduces a unified framework for systematically evaluating the robustness of ML models in power system protection. High-fidelity EMT simulations are used to model realistic degradation scenarios, including sensor outages, reduced sampling rates, and transient communication losses. The framework provides a consistent methodology for benchmarking models, quantifying the impact of limited observability, and identifying critical measurement channels required for resilient operation. Results show that FC remains highly stable under most degradation types but drops by about 13% under single-phase loss, while FL is more sensitive overall, with current loss increasing localization error by over 150%. These findings offer actionable guidance for robustness-aware design of future ML-assisted protection systems.
Signal Processing.comment: This paper is a postprint of a paper submitted to and accepted for publication in the 20th IET International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP Global 2026) and is subject to Institution of Engineering and Technology Copyright. The copy of record is available at the IET Digital Library. V2 corrects current/voltage labels, the case count, and references

Signal Processing.title: Interference-Free In-Symbol Pilots for High-Mobility DFT-s-OFDM Uplink
Signal Processing.summary: The 5G New Radio (NR) uplink uses discrete Fourier transform spread orthogonal frequency-division multi- plexing (DFT-s-OFDM) for its low peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). Its demodulation reference signal (DMRS) occupies whole symbols, although channel estimation only needs channel samples. Since existing designs cannot place pilots inside a data symbol without interference on the data, or on both data and pilots, NR keeps whole DMRS symbols, which wastes spectral efficiency (SE), and adds more of them as the channel varies faster, lowering the SE further. We develop a technique that places pilots free of data interference inside the data symbols, for frequency-domain channel estimation in every symbol. Using the Zak transform, we show that leaving a set of equally spaced pre- DFT samples empty frees one column of the Zak grid of the DFT output. The data values of the pilot subcarriers are relocated into this column by adding a constant over a few subcarrier combs, which preserves the energy and keeps the NR DFT sizes. The receiver undoes it linearly with comb sums, without decisions or side information, and a symbol loses as few as one data sample beyond its pilots. Since the pilots raise the PAPR, we keep them few per symbol and hop their positions across symbols, so that a two-dimensional estimator over the slot resolves long delay spreads at high Doppler. On 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) channels, pilots in every symbol achieve a higher effective SE than all NR DMRS configurations from pedestrian to high- speed-train velocities, at a PAPR close to plain DFT-s-OFDM.
Signal Processing.comment: 10 pages, 8 figures

Signal Processing.title: Dual-Pilot Design for OCDM Channel Estimation
Signal Processing.summary: Channel acquisition in orthogonal chirp division multiplexing (OCDM) over doubly-dispersive channels incurs a large pilot overhead, since delay and Doppler jointly shift the symbols in the chirp domain and separating them requires repeated pilots, each protected against the complete coupled displacement. This letter proposes a dual-pulsone pilot design that reduces this overhead in two steps. First, a pulsone occupies fewer chirp-domain bins than alias-free Doppler estimation requires, deliberately allowing Doppler wrapping. Second, a phase-offset pulsone is placed within the same protected region to observe a complementary part of the displacement, further reducing the shared guard. The phase offset also resolves the wrapping ambiguity, enabling low-complexity delay-Doppler estimation. Simulations show competitive estimation and BER performance, with the lowest complexity and highest payload efficiency among the considered OCDM estimators.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 6 figures

Signal Processing.title: Sequences for Flat-Top Beams
Signal Processing.summary: Flat-top beams have numerous applications in radar and communication systems. Sequences with diverging merit factors can approach the ideal omnidirectional beams but do not directly apply to flat-top beams, which require simultaneous control of passband ripple and stopband leakage. To bridge this gap, we study the asymptotic behavior of both quantities of flat-top beams by using tools of Fourier analysis. We establish contrasting results for sequences with finite or infinite alphabets. For sequences with finite alphabet, including binary and quaternary ones, their passband ripple and stopband leakage cannot simultaneously vanish as the sequence length grows to infinity. For sequences with infinite alphabet, however, both requirements are satisfied simultaneously by the generalized step-chirp (GSC) sequences if and only if the length-bandwidth product $Nγ$ goes to infinity and the distance of the step size $a$ from $\{0,1,\tfrac12,\tfrac13,\ldots\}$ goes to zero. Besides, both quantities vanish at rate $O((Nγ)^{-1/2})$ if $a\in \{1,\tfrac12,\tfrac13,\ldots\}$.These results broaden the scope of classical sequence design beyond full-band spectral flatness and provide a theoretical foundation for flat-top beam synthesis.

Signal Processing.title: DBFM: Dual-Band Flow Matching for ECG Super-Resolution
Signal Processing.summary: Long-term ECG monitoring is increasingly supported by wearable and portable devices, where limited power and transmission capacity motivate acquisition at lower sampling rates. ECG super-resolution (SR) aims to reconstruct high-sampling-rate signals from low-sampling-rate recordings for clinical analysis. A recent diffusion-based approach, DiSR-ECG, has demonstrated powerful reconstruction performance, particularly in cross-dataset evaluation. However, its iterative sampling during inference incurs high computational cost when processing large volumes of long-term ECG data. To reduce this cost while maintaining reconstruction accuracy, we propose Dual-Band Flow Matching (DBFM), a generative framework for ECG SR. DBFM decomposes ECG signals into low- and high-frequency components and separately learns their source-to-target transport using conditional flow matching. This dual-band formulation enables frequency-specific reconstruction, while one-step inference substantially reduces computational complexity. Experimental results show that DBFM achieves performance comparable to or better than DiSR-ECG while reducing inference FLOPs by approximately 98.7\%. These results demonstrate that DBFM enables computationally efficient ECG SR without compromising reconstruction quality.

Signal Processing.title: Impact of Data Sparsity on Machine Learning for Fault Detection in Power System Protection
Signal Processing.summary: Germany's transition to a renewable energy-based power system is reshaping grid operations, requiring advanced monitoring and control to manage decentralized generation. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a powerful tool for power system protection, particularly for fault detection (FD) and fault line identification (FLI) in transmission grids. However, ML model reliability depends on data quality and availability. Data sparsity resulting from sensor failures, communication disruptions, or reduced sampling rates poses a challenge to ML-based FD and FLI. Yet, its impact has not been systematically validated prior to this work. In response, we propose a framework to assess the impact of data sparsity on ML-based FD and FLI performance. We simulate realistic data sparsity scenarios, evaluate their impact, derive quantitative insights, and demonstrate the effectiveness of this evaluation strategy by applying it to an existing ML-based framework. After 50-fold decimation, the model achieves an F1-score of 0.999 $\pm$ 0.000 for FD. For FLI, removing current measurements reduces the F1-score by 55.61%, and the Bus 2 loss scenario reduces it by 9.73%. These results quantify the sensitivity of the two tasks to the evaluated input restrictions.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 2 figures. Corrected current and voltage ablation labels and summary statistics. Clarified the communication-gap and downsampling protocols

Signal Processing.title: Integrated Semantic Sensing and Communications: Target Attribute Inference and Beamforming Design
Signal Processing.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is expected to become a key enabling paradigm for future 6G networks, supporting emerging applications that require a comprehensive understanding of sensed targets. As a step toward this goal, we consider an ISAC system with semantic sensing capability that determines what the sensed target is, where it is located, and how large it is. However, the accurate retrieval of these attributes, including target class, location, and size, is challenging due to the highly nonlinear relationships between the received signals and different attributes. In addition, new beamforming strategies are also required to balance multi-user communication and semantic sensing performance. To address the first challenge, we develop a physics-guided inference model that leverages signal propagation priors and a unified Transformer backbone to effectively characterize the highly nonlinear relationships between received ISAC signals and multiple attributes. As for the second challenge, we develop a multi-stage training framework for the optimization of beamformers and model parameters, aiming to improve semantic sensing performance while guaranteeing multi-user communication requirements. Simulation results show that under the same multi-user communication rate requirements, the proposed scheme can provide more than 12% performance gains across classification, localization, and size estimation tasks compared with existing methods and achieve 91.21% classification accuracy using only two OFDM frames, demonstrating the feasibility of accurate semantic sensing with low measurement overhead.

Signal Processing.title: CRISP: Sparse Risk-Calibrated Front-End Allocation and Fusion for Low-Resolution Snapshot GNSS Positioning
Signal Processing.summary: Low-resolution global navigation satellite system snapshot receivers face strong coupling among automatic gain control compression, coarse quantization, and waveform distortion from nonlinear interference mitigation. This paper presents Cross-Risk Interference-Resilient Snapshot Positioning, denoted CRISP, an aided single-snapshot architecture that allocates and fuses complementary pre-correlation processors over a bounded position-clock search region under a shared direct position estimation solve budget. On a pre-frozen baseband descriptor partition, offline calibration estimates uncentered second-order position-error cross moments and solves cardinality-constrained simplex programs along east, north, and up axes, retaining validation-screened multibranch combinations while assigning single matched processors elsewhere. An online reliability gate screens the same quantized snapshot to route unfamiliar waveforms toward single-branch protective operators. We characterize profiled contrast shifts after nonlinear suppression and derive a conditional finite-sample excess-risk bound across disjoint splits alongside an exact same-snapshot gating risk identity. Across 17 568 simulated 2-ms GPS L1 C/A trials, CRISP reduces core positioning root-mean-square error by 13.84%, > 100-m gross errors by 41.32%, and multi-geometry error by 12.23% over Snapshot-FD at 1.43 core and 1.51 overall solves per snapshot.

Signal Processing.title: Confidence-Aware Speed-over-Ground Estimation from Doppler Spectra via Reconstruction-Based Representation Learning
Signal Processing.summary: Reliable speed-over-ground estimation from ground-facing Doppler spectra is essential for mobile platforms such as railway systems. Classical signal-processing approaches can provide accurate estimates under favorable conditions, but often degrade in challenging conditions. We propose confidence-aware speed-over-ground estimation trained on rail-domain data that estimates speed over ground and frame-level confidence from Doppler spectra with several novel contributions: First, we transfer the idea of exploiting a reconstruction task by an autoencoder for performance estimation from previous work to Doppler RaDAR. Second, we append a speed-over-ground estimation head operating on the autoencoder's latent space features. Third, we omit the reconstruction decoder during inference but add a low-cost dedicated confidence head for frame-wise error-bound estimation. Fourth, we reveal how noise augmentation training can provide high robustness to the method. Experiments show that our approach improves speed estimation accuracy over classical baselines while providing informative confidence estimates that indicate the reliability of individual predictions, even under adverse signal conditions.

Signal Processing.title: Net-Gain-Optimized Constellation Shaping for the 5G NR DFT-s-OFDM Uplink: Probabilistic, Geometric, and Joint Designs
Signal Processing.summary: Constellation shaping improves the achievable information rate of coded modulation. On the single-carrier uplink waveform of 5G New Radio, discrete Fourier transform (DFT)- spread orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), the same shaping can also raise the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). A higher PAPR forces more power amplifier back- off and reduces the link budget. Prior work characterized this penalty for fixed probabilistically and geometrically shaped constellations, but did not turn the trade-off into a design objective. We optimize constellation shaping (CS) to maximize the net-gain, i.e., the sum of the communication gain and the PAPR gain, at the fixed spectral efficiency of 4 bits per channel use for 64-QAM. We apply it to probabilistic shaping (PS), geometric shaping (GS), and a joint scheme that combines both. As the coded block error rate cannot be evaluated inside a gradient loop, we use the achievable information rate as a surrogate for the communication performance and the PAPR surrogate as differentiable cost functions for the optimizer. The learned constellations are then validated on a complete DFT-s-OFDM link-level chain. Conventional Maxwell-Boltzmann PS yields a negative net-gain, but net-gain-aware optimization removes this deficit in every method. GS converts it into a substantial gain, as it not only improves the communication performance but also lowers the PAPR below the uniform 64-QAM reference, achieving the largest net-gain among the CS methods studied.
Signal Processing.comment: Submitted to WCNC2027

Signal Processing.title: Strategic Beam Brainstorming for Generative Site-Specific Beamforming
Signal Processing.summary: A novel plug-and-play candidate beam selection strategy is proposed for generative site-specific beamforming (GenSSBF), a paradigm that draws on a learned conditional channel distribution to generate multiple plausible beams. Under a limited probing budget, realizing the full potential of GenSSBF requires identifying which candidate beams are worth probing. To this end, the marginal probing value is first derived to guide strategic candidate probing by quantifying each beam's additional gain beyond those already selected. Based on this criterion, two algorithms are developed without retraining the generator: 1) Greedy candidate probing (GCP) selects all candidate beams from a locally generated pool prior to over-the-air probing, requiring only a single feedback round; 2) Adaptive candidate probing (ACP) exploits reference signal received power (RSRP) feedback after each probe to update channel hypothesis weights and guide the next beam selection, without increasing the asymptotic complexity. Simulations across three ray-tracing scenarios under noiseless and noisy probing reveal that: 1) candidate complementarity is key to efficient beam brainstorming; and 2) ACP is particularly beneficial when initial sensing leaves substantial channel uncertainty and subsequent feedback is reliable.

Signal Processing.title: PhysRF-WorldJEPA: Transforming Heterogeneous Large Language Models into Manifold-Decoupled Millimeter-Wave Radar World Models
Signal Processing.summary: Adapting Large Language Models (LLMs) to millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar enables privacy-preserving, all-weather physical scene understanding across darkness, smoke, and walls. However, standard instruction tuning treats continuous radar streams as static text-like tokens, causing near-random global radar-to-text retrieval and severe physical drift under sensor blackouts. Conversely, coupling pairwise contrastive losses (e.g., SigLIP) directly into the shared backbone improves retrieval but injects $O(B^2)$ repulsive gradients that fracture continuous coordinate manifolds ($R^2 < 0$). We present PhysRF-WorldJEPA, a manifold-decoupled Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) that separates continuous electromagnetic state prediction from cross-modal language alignment. An unattenuated 1.0x clock anchor and parallel dual-scale RF encoder feed a lean ~3% LoRA LLM trained with two-step state-space EMA-JEPA (Denoise -> Rollout) and sample-axis Batch-VICReg to predict +3.0 s physical states; a stop-gradient alignment head then maps frozen prompt states onto the text hypersphere with false-negative masking. On a 4,541-window tri-domain suite (77/60.25/60 GHz) against 10 baselines, freezing the physical backbone and training only the decoupled head lifts R->T R@10 from 5.95% to 15.01% and improves MedRank from 107.0 to 60.0 while preserving identical physical readout: 3.37 deg ($R^2=+0.961$) blackout +3.0 s torso tilt, 1.89 m ($R^2=+0.679$; 1.19 m/+0.863 at the RF front-end) cluttered UAV altitude, 2.04 m ($R^2=+0.461$) behind-wall NLOS range, 0.9976 virtual-RIS invariance, and 100% fall recall. Across five 0.5B-1.8B LLM families (15 zero-overhead models), World-JEPA improves retrieval and 75%-drop completion in 10/10 runs and blackout tilt in 4/5 (Span-Euc), 2/5 (Scatter), and 5/5 (per-family best) over SFT.
Signal Processing.comment: 11 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables

Signal Processing.title: Wireless-OptSG: A Versatile Multi-Agent Optimization Framework for Wireless Resource Allocation
Signal Processing.summary: 6G wireless networks are expected to accommodate heterogeneous service requirements across diverse deployment scenarios, giving rise to physical-layer resource allocation problems with scenario-dependent objectives and constraints. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and agent systems can interpret wireless-domain specifications and incorporate execution feedback into optimization. However, translating language-level reasoning into feasible, high-quality resource allocations remains challenging, since candidates need to satisfy precise mathematical constraints throughout iterative search. This work proposes the Wireless Optimization Solution Generator (Wireless-OptSG), a versatile multi-agent framework for physical-layer resource allocation. Wireless-OptSG organizes optimization as a feedback-driven candidate search guided by a static meta-prompt and an evolving optimization history. In a nested outer-inner loop, parallel agents explore solution trajectories and periodically exchange high-quality records to guide candidate generation. Feasible initialization uses executable optimization primitives, while a tiered repair pipeline restores feasibility and solution-dependent context improves retained-record informativeness. Experiments on four representative tasks under perfect and imperfect channel state information show that Wireless-OptSG achieves performance comparable to scenario-specific state-of-the-art (SOTA) solvers, exceeds SOTA in some settings, and consistently outperforms generic baselines, demonstrating its potential as a transferable optimization framework for future wireless networks.
Signal Processing.comment: 13 pages, 8 figures, 4 tables

Signal Processing.title: EEGJev: A System One Decision Model and Benchmark for Multi-Task EEG Question Answering
Signal Processing.summary: A single electroencephalographic (EEG) recording can support multiple decoding tasks. Fixed-label tests cannot show how EEG foundation models handle changing questions or options. We introduce EEGJev, a fast decision model that scores candidate answers in one pass. Our benchmark, EEGJev-Bench, covers six question types across 19 public EEG sources. We held the recording and options fixed while switching between questions about attributes paired during training, such as facial expression and the hand participants were asked to use. Across 13 test sources, EEGJev selected a label for the requested attribute with 99.70% accuracy (49.20% under uniform choice). Balanced accuracy for the specific answer was 62.04%. Its 95th-percentile response time was shorter than NeuroLM's on matched validation questions answered individually. EEGJev lets users switch decoding targets by changing the question. With EEGJev-Bench, researchers can test whether new decoders follow the question more reliably, identify the correct answer more often, or both.
Signal Processing.comment: 28 pages, 6 figures. Includes supplementary information

Signal Processing.title: Model Order Detection with Parameter Estimation Guarantees for the Matrix Pencil Method
Signal Processing.summary: Detecting the model order and estimating the parameters of sums of damped complex exponentials in noise is challenging when poles are closely spaced, the sample size is small, or the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is low. We propose REECAP, a matrix pencil (MP) algorithm for joint model order detection and pole estimation. The algorithm computes candidate poles using an overestimated working rank and classifies them using a score derived from their associated eigenvectors. The model order is then estimated by counting the retained candidates. The score measures the eigenvector energy concentration in coordinates corresponding to the dominant right singular subspace of the data Hankel matrix. Under a suitable rank condition, we derive a deterministic sufficient condition guaranteeing that a candidate whose score exceeds a certain threshold lies within a prescribed tolerance of at least one signal pole. This establishes a theoretical connection between eigenvector energy concentration and pole-estimation accuracy. Extensive simulations demonstrate improved model order detection and frequency estimation performance relative to conventional MP order detection methods, recent structure-aware MP methods, and information-theoretic criteria (ITC), across a broad range of scenarios, including clustered frequencies, low SNR in the threshold region, and small sample sizes. Runtime comparisons further demonstrate substantial computational savings, and moderate sensitivity to noise model mismatch, compared to the evaluated structure-aware and information-theoretic methods.

Signal Processing.title: HAPS-Complemented Terrestrial Networks
Signal Processing.summary: We consider a downlink multicell multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system in an urban region, with a focus on improving the capacity of cell-edge user equipments (UEs). These UEs typically experience lower rates than near UEs because of shadowing, path loss, and inter-cell interference (ICI). To address this issue, we integrate a high-altitude platform station (HAPS) with the terrestrial network as a relay for edge-UE transmissions. We assume that the HAPS operates in full-duplex (FD) mode and exploits its large physical size to enhance passive self-interference (SI) suppression by separating its transmit and receive antennas. In the proposed scheme, each terrestrial base station (BS) forwards edge-UE data to the FD-HAPS, which then relays the data to the intended edge UEs. To design beams at both BSs and HAPS, we formulate an {edge-UE} sum-rate maximization problem under total transmit-power and minimum quality-of-service (QoS) constraints. To solve the resulting non-convex problem, we develop a centralized algorithm based on successive convex approximation (SCA) and alternating optimization (AO) for fast convergence. Simulation results show that relaying information via FD-HAPS significantly improves the capacity of cell-edge UEs compared with a terrestrial-only network.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, accepted for publication in the proceedings of IEEE CCNC-2027

Signal Processing.title: Multi-User Linear Precoder Optimization for Obfuscation-Aided Mixed Regular and Wiretap Coding
Signal Processing.summary: Physical-layer security has attracted considerable research interest with the development of quantum computing. One prominent approach is wiretap coding, which exploits the channel advantage of a legitimate receiver over an eavesdropper to achieve secure communication. However, under unfavorable channel conditions, wiretap coding can significantly reduce the achievable rate compared to regular channel coding. Mixed coding alleviates this limitation by using wiretap coding to protect a short secret required for obfuscation, while the obfuscated payload is encoded using regular channel coding. In this work, we propose a generalized obfuscation-aided mixed-coding system based on the multi-user (MU)-linear precoding (LP) architecture that unifies existing approaches employing different obfuscation functions. We then formulate the corresponding precoder optimization problem, abstracting the obfuscation function through a minimum secrecy rate constraint. Numerical simulations using a geometric two-user line-of-sight (LoS) channel demonstrated how the minimum secrecy rate requirement determines the operating point of mixed coding between regular and wiretap coding. Subsequent beampattern analysis revealed a key synergy between mixed coding and precoding: Mixed coding enables individual beam shaping for the two coding layers. Finally, spatial analysis showed that mixed coding offers the largest sum-rate gains when users are positioned at similar angles.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages + 7 pages appendix, 6 figures, 3 tables, 1 algorithm. Extended version of the manuscript submitted to IEEE WCNC 2027, including the detailed derivation of the SCA algorithm

Signal Processing.title: Modeling Lunar Power Harvesting and Battery Recharging In The Presence of Random Pointing Error
Signal Processing.summary: In our work, we establish a lunar power beaming environment between a low-lunar orbiter and a circular solar panel mounted on top of a lunar vehicle located at the Lunar South Pole. Due to the random nature of the pointing errors, various upper bounds reflecting the severity of these errors are considered. Although harvested power is modelled stochastically in the literature, we extend this randomness to battery-storage analysis by deriving PDFs of state of charge, accumulated battery capacity and energy, and end-to-end efficiency for both battery charging modes. Then, our derivations are verified with extensive Monte Carlo simulations. Hence, our derivations provide a mathematical model that enables prediction and helps us understand the randomness of the corresponding variables. For the given pointing error levels, we quantify the differences between charging modes in these battery metrics. Our work explains the stochastic nature of these battery metrics in a realistic lunar environment. Regarding the end-to-end efficiency metric, which is the ratio of the stored electrical energy to the transmitted electrical energy, we observed that slow-charging efficiency is immune to pointing errors, and this mode can utilize only one-sixth of what the link can deliver under a mild pointing error.
Signal Processing.comment: 12 pages

Signal Processing.title: Direct-to-Cell Satellite Communications: Task-Oriented Paradigm for 6G Closed-Loop Autonomous Operations
Signal Processing.summary: Direct-to-cell (D2C) satellite communications have emerged as a crucial alternative to terrestrial communications in the sixth generation (6G) mobile networks due to their wide-area coverage capability. Unlike human-oriented communications, future 6G robot-oriented D2C satellite communications in autonomous operations place greater emphasis on the ultimate task completion than on the intermediate stage of data transmissions. Such a difference renders it crucial to evaluate the performance of each stage in a systematic manner and consider a multistage integrated optimization. Motivated by this, we model the system with a sensing-communication-computing-control (SC3) closed loop and analyze it from an entropy-based perspective, from which a task-oriented system design method is developed. Furthermore, to manage the complexity of the closed-loop network, we decompose it into fine-grained functional structures and investigate the key challenges of collaborative sensing, collaborative computing, and collaborative control. A case study is presented to compare the proposed task-oriented scheme with conventional communication-oriented schemes, showing that the proposed method has better performance in system-level control cost. Finally, several open issues are outlined for future research and practical implementation.

Systems and Control.title: Model Predictive Control of a Multirotor UAV with a Cable-Suspended Payload: A Comparison of Shifted and Transformer-Based Warm Starts
Systems and Control.summary:
This study investigates model predictive control (MPC) of a multirotor drone (unmanned aerial vehicle, UAV) carrying a cable-suspended payload, comparing conventional shifted initialization with Transformer-based warm starting of a sequential convex programming (SCP) optimizer. The controller uses a coupled mechanical model with an elastic cable and a double-pendulum representation of the suspended load. Its formulation includes move-blocked control inputs, finite-difference sensitivities, constrained quadratic subproblems, and input-feasibility projection. A Transformer trained on expert SCP solutions predicts an initial control sequence, which is subsequently refined by the same optimizer used for the conventional methods. Numerical experiments compare zero, shifted, and Transformer initialization under identical controller settings. For independently solved MPC problems, Transformer initialization reduces computation time relative to zero initialization. In sequential closed-loop simulations, however, shifting the preceding optimized control sequence provides the lowest computation time, while all three methods produce similar tracking behavior. These findings emphasize the importance of comparing learned warm starts with conventional initialization methods that reuse previous MPC solutions. The measured optimization times exceed the control sampling period; consequently, real-time implementation is not demonstrated.
  Keywords: Model predictive control; sequential convex programming; Transformer; warm start; cable-suspended payload; multirotor drone.
Systems and Control.comment: 13 pages, 11 figures, 4 tables

Systems and Control.title: MVDC Power Cables for Future Wide-Body All-Electric Aircraft: A Research Journey from System-Level Requirements to Modeling, Design, Fabrication, and Testing
Systems and Control.summary: Future wide-body all-electric aircraft require lightweight electrical distribution systems capable of delivering megawatt-scale propulsion power under demanding thermal and electrical conditions. This article reviews our research program on medium-voltage direct-current (MVDC) power cables, from aircraft-level requirements through modeling, design, fabrication, and low-pressure electrical testing. It connects successive investigations and explains the decisions guiding their development. Aircraft-level power-flow and single-contingency studies establish a +/-5 kV distribution architecture and a 1 kA design objective for the most heavily loaded cable circuits. Coupled electrical, thermal, and airflow models examine multilayer multifunctional electrical insulation, conductor geometry, bipolar pole spacing, duct configuration, and forced convection. Flight-phase studies distinguish higher-current takeoff operation from lower-current operation at reduced cruise pressure. Experiments progress from bonded flat specimens to wrapped cable prototypes, examining fabrication methods, partial discharge, and dielectric breakdown at atmospheric pressure and pressures down to 18.8 kPa. The results highlight the roles of insulation interfaces, wrapping method, cable geometry, and installation conditions in achieving compact designs with improved electrical performance. Together, these studies provide a development framework linking aircraft requirements to manufacturable prototypes. Predicted current-carrying capability is distinguished from measured insulation performance, and the combined electrical, thermal, mechanical, and endurance evaluations needed for aircraft qualification are identified.

Systems and Control.title: Discovering Explicit Magnetic Core-Loss Equations via Symbolic Sparse Identification
Systems and Control.summary: Compact core loss equations are essential tools in magnetic component design, but existing approaches trade accuracy against interpretability. Empirical models such as the Steinmetz Equation (SE) yield compact expressions of limited accuracy, while machine learning methods achieve high accuracy as black-box predictors. This paper bridges the gap with a Symbolic Sparse Identification (SSI) framework, which casts core loss modeling as a data-driven symbolic regression problem and recovers unknown equations directly from measured data, without presuming a functional form. First, a comprehensively expanded library of symbolic candidate terms far richer than the SE is constructed. Second, the governing terms are isolated from this library by sparse regression. Third, the coefficients of the retained terms are refined with an AdamW optimizer to maximize accuracy and form an analytical equation. Experiments on Fair-Rite 78, 79, and 95 yield test mean absolute percentage errors of 1.89%, 1.01%, and 1.56%, respectively, with only 10, 10, and 7 active terms. Comparisons with empirical, numerical, and symbolic models quantify the resulting balance of accuracy and compactness. SSI thus provides an explicit and physically guided approach for high-frequency magnetic characterization and design.

Systems and Control.title: Global Exponential and Inverse Optimal Stabilization of a 3D Nonholonomic Vehicle in Spherical Coordinates
Systems and Control.summary: For the 3D nonholonomic vehicle actuated in surge velocity, pitch rate, and yaw rate, we construct continuous time-invariant feedback laws that stabilize both the roll-free and roll-augmented kinematic models to a target position and orientation in spherical coordinates. The design uses a spherical coordinate transformation with a singular set of codimension two and measure zero. We first present a backstepping design that yields explicit unidirectional, cusp-free feedback laws and strict barrier control Lyapunov functions (CLFs). These establish global exponential stability in spherical coordinates with user-assigned decay rates, while ensuring bounded Cartesian trajectories and exponential convergence to the target, consistent with Brockett's obstruction. The barrier terms guarantee avoidance of the coordinate singularities away from the target. The strict CLFs are then used to develop families of asymptotically stabilizing inverse optimal feedback laws for both systems that minimize a meaningful infinite-horizon cost. These laws inherit infinite gain margins from driftlessness, respect user-defined input bounds through Legendre-Fenchel transformations, and are implementable with either bidirectional or unidirectional surge actuation. Two penalty choices are illustrated: a quadratic input penalty whose associated state running cost approaches a prescribed quadratic form, and an input-constraining penalty that enforces user-defined bounds. This paper lays the foundation for constructive stabilization of the 3D nonholonomic vehicle.
Systems and Control.comment: Journal version, submitted to IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control. Unifies and extends two conference papers: v1 of this entry (accepted to the 2026 IEEE Conference on Decision and Control) and arXiv:2609.36212 (submitted to the 2027 American Control Conference), which this version supersedes. v1 remains available as the CDC conference version. 16 pages, 7 figures

Systems and Control.title: Fuel-Efficient Formation Flying via Constrained Extremum Seeking
Systems and Control.summary: This paper presents a model-free autonomous guidance architecture for minimal drag of a trailing aircraft in formation flight. Realizing the fuel savings resulting from such a formation requires learning and tracking a time-varying vortex while avoiding locations where the aircraft experiences an abrupt rolling moment disturbance. A guidance architecture for fuel-efficient safe flight, called Adaptive Plateau-seeking Optimal Guidance with ModulatEd Excitations (APOGEE), is proposed herein. Key features of APOGEE are its ability to modulate the amplitude of the excitation required to learn the unknown objective and constraint functions, to adaptively adjust the learning rates, and to keep the flight safe during the search for the optimal formation. A threshold-gated modulation reduces the amplitude of excitation when the objective function reaches an acceptably large value, thus improving flying qualities and further reducing fuel consumption. Furthermore, a Newton-based learning rule, whose estimate of the inverse of the Hessian is spectrally clamped, adapts the learning rates to the local curvature of the objective function in order to accelerate convergence and lower the chance of overshooting the optimum. Finally, a safety filter having an unknown constraint function is used to prevent a loss of control event prompted by the above mentioned disturbance. The efficacy of APOGEE is demonstrated by using a high-fidelity model of an F-16 jet and an experimentally obtained vortex model. Being model-free, APOGEE does not require modeling the dependence of the unknown functions on the characteristics of the leading aircraft, the flight condition, the crosswind, and the vortex-induced turbulence.
Systems and Control.comment: Submitted to the 2027 American Control Conference (ACC), 8 pages, 6 figures

Systems and Control.title: Voltage-Feedback Backoff and Restoration for Priority-Based EV Charging Control
Systems and Control.summary: Uncoordinated residential electric vehicle (EV) charging can cause sustained undervoltage in distribution networks. This paper proposes a centralized voltage-feedback backoff and restoration (VFBR) framework that separates concurrent charging-count control from EV selection. The controller adjusts the allowable charging count using monitored critical-bus voltages, without load forecasts, online power-flow calculations, or optimization. Initial charging suspension relieves undervoltage, followed by group-wise restoration and backoff as voltage conditions permit. A complementary priority score combines charging urgency with voltage sensitivity precomputed offline to balance time-critical requests against their location-dependent voltage impacts. One-week simulations on the unbalanced IEEE 123-bus feeder with 500 EVs show that VFBR reduces the proportion of charging-period bus-time samples below 0.95 p.u. from 15% to less than 1%. Among the evaluated strategies, combined allocation with urgency and sensitivity weights of 0.75 and 0.25 delivers 25% more energy than random allocation and achieves the highest mean departure state of charge and fairness. These results demonstrate that simple voltage-feedback control, coupled with urgency- and sensitivity-based allocation, effectively mitigates undervoltage while improving charging service.
Systems and Control.comment: 5 pages, 6 figures

Systems and Control.title: Topology-Aware Congestion Pricing: Demand Robust Routing using the Forman-Ricci Curvature
Systems and Control.summary: Congestion pricing is widely used to improve transportation network efficiency where individual decentralized route choices can lead to system-level inefficiencies. Pigouvian tolls achieve the system optimum but depend on demand and can lose effectiveness under demand shifts, particularly on structurally critical bottleneck edges. We propose a topology-aware regularization of the Beckmann potential governing the (Wardrop) equilibrium by augmenting precomputed Pigouvian tolls with an offline structural penalty derived from Forman--Ricci curvature (FRC), which captures bottleneck structures. We prove that the resulting equilibrium is well-defined, that stronger regularization reduces flow on penalized edges, and that efficiency loss depends on how closely the structural penalty approximates optimal Pigouvian tolls. Experiments on eight real-world networks under targeted and uniform demand perturbations show reduced bottleneck flow with near-optimal efficiency. FRC achieves reductions comparable to edge betweenness at substantially lower computational cost, making it a practical, robust complement to classical congestion pricing.

Systems and Control.title: Posterior error bounds for prior-driven balancing in linear Gaussian inverse problems
Systems and Control.summary: In large-scale Bayesian inverse problems, it is often necessary to apply approximate forward models to reduce the cost of forward model evaluations, while controlling approximation quality. In the context of Bayesian inverse problems with linear forward models, Gaussian priors, and Gaussian noise, we use perturbation theory for inverses to bound the error in the approximate posterior mean and posterior covariance resulting from a linear approximate forward model. We then focus on the smoothing problem of inferring the initial condition of linear time-invariant dynamical systems, using finitely many partial state observations. For such problems, and for a specific model order reduction method based on balanced truncation, we show that the impulse response of a certain prior-driven system is closely related to the prior-preconditioned Hessian of the inverse problem. This reveals a novel connection between systems theory and inverse problems. We exploit this connection to prove the first a priori error bounds for system-theoretic model order reduction methods applied to smoothing problems. The bounds control the approximation error of the posterior mean and covariance in terms of the truncated Hankel singular values of the underlying system.

Systems and Control.title: From Safety-Driven Redundancy to Value-Driven Architecture: An ODD-Based Rationalization Framework for Level 4 Autonomous Vehicles
Systems and Control.summary: Level 4 autonomous vehicles require fault-tolerant architectures that preserve critical driving functions under sensing, computing, communication, power, and actuation failures. As these systems progress toward industrial scalability, architectural complexity, validation burden, integration effort, and lifecycle cost become increasingly relevant. This study proposes an Operational Design Domain (ODD)-based, safety-constrained systems-engineering framework for architecture rationalization. ODD-specific capabilities, physical fault assumptions, post-fault operational policies, and spatial sensing requirements are propagated through an integrated safety-feasibility gate. Architecture transformations, including removal, relocation, functional reassignment, and consolidation, are evaluated only within the resulting safety-feasible design space, followed by lifecycle-cost sensitivity and robust multiobjective Pareto analysis. A generic, synthetically parameterized Level 4 architecture is used as a demonstrative computational case study. Within this modeled design space, direct ablation showed limited rationalization potential, whereas directional redistribution and functional consolidation generated a broader set of safety-feasible candidates. Under the illustrative lifecycle-cost model, the best nominal candidate achieved a 5.55% normalized cost reduction and remained cost-reducing across all 5,000 sampled points in the prescribed uncertainty domain. The analysis identified 15 non-dominated architecture-policy solutions representing seven physical transformations. The results support capability-based, policy-conditioned, and lifecycle-aware architecture rationalization under the stated assumptions, with safety retained as a non-compensatory feasibility constraint. The reported transformations are design candidates rather than validated production architectures.
Systems and Control.comment: 17 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables. Report number

Systems and Control.title: An exponential-rate consensus-based algorithms for estimation from relative measurements: implementation and performance analysis
Systems and Control.summary: In this work we address the problem of optimal estimating the position of each agent in a network from relative noisy vectorial distances with its neighbors. Although the problem can be cast as a standard least-squares problem, the main challenge is to devise scalable algorithms that allow each agent to estimate its own position by means of only local communication and bounded complexity, independently of the network size and topology. We first propose a synchronous consensus-based algorithm that is guaranteed to have exponentially convergence rate to the optimal centralized least-squares solution. We then extend this algorithm to more realistic asynchronous implementations via the use of local memory variables. We show that exponential convergence is still guaranteed under both uniform persistent communication and randomized persistent communication protocols. We finally complement the analytical results with some numerical simulations.
Systems and Control.comment: 13 pages, 5 figures, Technical Report previously published at https://automatica.dei.unipd.it/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/consensus-based_localization_tech_note.pdf in 2013

Systems and Control.title: Compositional Reachset-Conformant Modeling for Managing Uncertainty in the Development of Cyber-Physical Systems
Systems and Control.summary: The development of cyber-physical systems (CPS) proceeds through iterative design revisions, and compliance with safety requirements must be re-established after every revision, typically based on a system model. Conventional models, however, predict only the most likely behavior, leading to model-plant mismatch that often surfaces only during late-stage testing, when redesign is most expensive. This article presents reachset-conformant modeling as a framework for managing uncertainty throughout the development process: instead of a single trajectory, a reachset-conformant model predicts a set of behaviors, calibrated from data to conservatively enclose the true system behavior with a statistical guarantee. Safety properties established on the model therefore transfer to the realized system. Beyond a practical introduction to reachset-conformant identification and its benefits for CPS development, our main theoretical contribution is a closure result: reachset conformance is preserved under serial composition, parallel composition, and feedback interconnection, and hence under any architecture assembled from these primitives. Subsystem models identified independently from local measurements can thus be substituted into the system architecture, and the interconnected model inherits a coverage guarantee from the subsystem guarantees. We complement this result with update strategies that adapt the uncertainty sets after design changes without restarting the identification workflow. Experiments on an automotive brake-system test bench demonstrate that a) a single model covers all operating conditions and hardware variants, b) late-stage modifications are absorbed by uncertainty set updates, c) a black-box hydraulic unit is conservatively abstracted from input-output data alone, and d) independently identified subsystem models form a conformant model by construction.
Systems and Control.comment: 24 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Under review

Systems and Control.title: Adaptive Electromagnetic Transient-level Digital Twins for Data Centers via In-Context Learning with LLMs
Systems and Control.summary: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads has significantly increased data center (DC) power demand. Frequent operational and configurational changes, such as load surges caused by dynamic workload allocation, can induce electromagnetic transients (EMTs) whose accurate prediction is critical for reliable DC operation and maintenance. Although high-fidelity EMT solvers are widely adopted for transient analysis, their computational cost limits large-scale and multi-scenario studies. Digital twins address this computational bottleneck by emulating the behavior of a physical system and enabling fast prediction in place of expensive high-fidelity simulation. However,data-driven digital twins are non-adaptive and fail to generalize once the DC configuration changes. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an adaptive EMT-level digital twin for DCs based on in-context learning (ICL) with large language models (LLMs). We formulate the EMT prediction task as a system identification problem under parametric uncertainty and develop a GPT-2-based framework that adapts to unseen DC configurations at inference time from a small set of EMT trajectory samples, without model retraining. The proposed framework is validated on three representative EMT scenarios and benchmarked against three baseline non-adaptive twins. Results demonstrate superior prediction accuracy, improved adaptability to unseen operating conditions, and substantial computational speedups compared to high-fidelity EMT simulation.
Systems and Control.comment: Under Review

Systems and Control.title: Space Postman and ATLAS: Enabling Startup Participation in the Orbital Logistics Economy
Systems and Control.summary: Debris removal, in-orbit servicing and refuelling, last-mile delivery, in-space recycling and constellation deployment are separate businesses built on one planning problem: a single spacecraft must visit many targets whose orbital planes drift apart under Earth's oblateness, within a propellant tank and a deadline. Solving it well takes orbital dynamics and optimisation expertise that is rarely the core business of payload, tug or constellation companies; this keeps young operators out of orbital logistics or leaves them with costly hand-made schedules. This paper presents Space Postman, a planning service that turns a target list, a spacecraft and a time budget into a priced and, for rendezvous tours, verified mission plan, and ATLAS, a tug concept whose payload bay takes debris kits, client spacecraft or propellant. As most start-ups fail when the money runs out, the offer starts with software and adds the vehicle later. Two case studies show what it changes. For a notional follow-on to the DEXTER project, which develops ways to turn scrap aluminium into propellant, it plans a tour of ten high-risk upper stages that share one orbital shell: waiting alone cannot close the tour, an even split of the time costs a third more propellant, and time is the currency of the mission. For a tug that releases eight clients from one rideshare, the delivery order decides whether the tank suffices, and the plan prices each delivery by the plane it must reach. The planning engine reproduces the published winning solution of a public debris-removal benchmark at that solution's fidelity and, given the same launches, plans cheaper trajectories for most of them: an independent check for operators and investors. A calibrated planner paired with a payload-agnostic tug offers new operators a practical way into orbital logistics, provided its numbers are read at the fidelity at which they were obtained.
Systems and Control.comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, 4 tables. Preprint of a paper accepted for presentation at the 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC 2026), Antalya, Türkiye, 5-9 October 2026 (IAF paper IAC-26,E6,1,10,x115070)

Systems and Control.title: Contract2Reach: Discretization-Induced Contractive Dynamic Programming for High-Dimensional Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability
Systems and Control.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) enable undiscounted Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability analysis for high-dimensional systems, but their performance can be sensitive to hyperparameter choices and the underlying system dynamics. We introduce Contract2Reach, which recasts undiscounted finite-horizon reachability as a sequence of contractive fixed-point problems solved by backward time marching. Our formulation combines discretized temporal and spatial derivatives to construct a contractive mapping without introducing a discount factor. Under standard assumptions, we prove that the exact scheme converges to the unique viscosity solution as both the temporal and spatial step sizes tend to zero. Unlike PINNs, our training fits rollout-based value targets via a single regression, without backpropagating through spatial value gradients. In the neural implementation, adaptive zero-level-set sampling and conservative target combination address high-dimensional sample sparsity and false positives, respectively. Experiments on a parameterized vertical drone, a 13D quadrotor, and a 40D publisher-subscriber system show competitive performance against PINNs-based baselines. Boundary evaluations on the vertical drone and publisher-subscriber systems demonstrate improved fidelity and reduced learning-rate sensitivity, revealing errors that volume-based metrics can miss.

Systems and Control.title: Convex computation of cost bounds for data-driven nonlinear optimal control
Systems and Control.summary: The paper addresses the optimal control problem of an input-affine polynomial system with an unknown (state-dependent) input matrix affecting the control effectiveness. Under assumptions on the existence of a data set and the Lipschitz continuity of the unknown part {of the dynamics}, an uncertainty set is constructed and used to adapt the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation towards a data-driven formulation. We solve it for the best-case scenario, thus giving a lower bound on the best cost achievable by means of a feedback control policy. After relaxing it into a moment-SoS hierarchy of semidefinite programs, a control law is extracted from the primal on moments and compared with other benchmark methods in a numerical application.

Systems and Control.title: Submodular Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Effective Online Distributed Task Allocation
Systems and Control.summary: This paper studies online distributed multi-agent task allocation with submodular team utilities. Since each agent selects one action from a local categorical distribution, feasible joint actions form a partition matroid over agent-action pairs. The classical Multilinear Extension relaxation, based on independent Bernoulli sampling, does not align with categorical execution under partition-matroid constraints. To remedy this, we propose the Partition Multilinear Extension (PME), which equals the expected stage utility under factorized categorical policies. We prove that submodular difference rewards provide unbiased PME marginal-gradient information and a stagewise policy-gradient estimator. Building on this connection, we propose SubMAPG, a centralized-training, decentralized-execution framework using masked categorical policies and difference-reward signals. For projected stochastic-gradient ascent in the PME marginal space, we establish a stagewise 1/2-approximation guarantee and sublinear dynamic regret under slowly varying environments. We instantiate SubMAPG on graph neural network policy models that effectively handle open systems with time-varying agents and tasks. Experiments on cooperative coverage and multi-target tracking showcase superior performance compared with standard MARL that does not leverage submodular rewards, online submodular optimization, and greedy baselines.
Systems and Control.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026

Systems and Control.title: From Reconnaissance to Response: Quantitative Risk Parameterization and Game Theoretic Containment in Modern Enterprise Attack
Systems and Control.summary: Modern Security Operations Centers struggle with delayed manual incident response, enabling adversaries to advance through the Cyber Kill Chain during early stage reconnaissance. While classical game theoretic defense models optimize strategic resource allocation, they rely on static utility matrices that fail to adapt to dynamic telemetry. This paper presents an integrated, metrics driven decision engine that bridges quantitative risk parameterization and continuous automated response time. Common Vulnerability Scoring Systems exploitability parameters are mapped to attacker success probabilities and evaluate defender log distributions via Factor Analysis of Information Risk Monte Carlo simulations. Real time SIEM logs streams are modeled as Poisson process arrival rates, dynamically updating defender posterior threat belief through sequential Bayesian filtering. A closed form threshold is derived by framing the interaction as a dynamic Bayesian Stackelberg game, where the expected unmitigated risk exceeds proactive containment cost. Parameterized against empirical data from the 2023 MGM Resorts and Caesars Entertainment cyber incident, simulation results demonstrate that the engine suppresses transient background noise while triggering automated SOAR network isolation within seconds of adversarial probing. Multi parameter sensitivity analysis confirms that the decision boundary dynamically adjusts to live perimeter vulnerability, offering a control theoretic foundation for sub minute automated threat containment.
Systems and Control.comment: 10 pages, 5 figures

Systems and Control.title: Automated Design and Evaluation Pipeline for Optimal Control Transcriptions in Model Predictive Control
Systems and Control.summary: The computational burden of Model Predictive Control represents a bottleneck limiting its widespread deployment in real-time applications. The selection of the optimal control transcription strategy for a given MPC formulation is a key driver of computational efficiency. Identifying performant MPC transcriptions requires significant effort and domain knowledge. We propose an automated pipeline for the design and evaluation of performant optimal control transcriptions for a given MPC formulation. Custom multi-objective design metrics, such as computation time or closed-loop performance, can be specified and are minimized by the pipeline. As a transcription method, a pseudospectral Legendre-Gauss-Radau method is employed. We show that it incorporates forward Euler integration and implicit collocation methods of low and high order in one formulation, leveraging the pipeline to evaluate both numerical approaches. Furthermore, different mesh configurations can be parameterized. To identify the optimal configuration of the transcription, a Bayesian Optimization framework is applied. The pipelines improvements in MPC performance are demonstrated through On-Orbit Servicing scenarios involving spacecraft motion planning and closed-loop control.

Systems and Control.title: Numerical benchmark for damage identification in Structural Health Monitoring
Systems and Control.summary: The availability of a dataset for validation and verification purposes of novel data-driven strategies and/or hybrid physics-data approaches is currently one of the most pressing challenges in the engineering field. Data ownership, security, access and metadata handiness are currently hindering advances across many fields, particularly in Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) applications. This paper presents a simulated SHM dataset, comprised of dynamic and static measurements (i.e., acceleration and displacement), and includes the conceptual framework designed to generate it. The simulated measurements were generated to incorporate the effects of Environmental and Operational Variations (EOVs), different types of damage, measurement noise and sensor faults and malfunctions, in order to account for scenarios that may occur during real acquisitions. A fixed-fixed steel beam structure was chosen as reference for the numerical benchmark. The simulated monitoring was operated under the assumptions of a Single Degree of Freedom (SDOF) for generating acceleration records and of the Euler-Bernoulli beam for the simulated displacement measurements. The generation process involved the use of parallel computation, which is detailed within the provided open-source code. The generated data is also available open-source, thus ensuring reproducibility, repeatability and accessibility for further research. Together, the openly available dataset and generation code provide a valuable resource for researchers aiming to develop, refine or compare SHM methods under controlled combinations of environmental, operational, structural, and measurement-related changes.
Systems and Control.comment: Submitted for peer review to Data Centric Engineering, Cambridge University Press

Systems and Control.title: Overparameterized Simulation-Error Minimization for Nonlinear System Identification: Horizon-Uniform Landscape and Identifiability
Systems and Control.summary: Simulation-error minimization is a standard criterion in nonlinear system identification, but its landscape is nonconvex and its conditioning can degrade geometrically with the data horizon N. We propose to lift the trajectory with a free, softly penalized per-step correction, which yields a fit loss that gradient descent provably minimizes: under a rank condition on the output map and a bound on the one-step Jacobian, it satisfies a Polyak-Lojasiewicz inequality with an explicit constant independent of N. A zero-loss model leaves the physical parameter undetermined. Identifiability is restored by a minimal-correction selection principle: under structural identifiability, the global minimizer of the penalized loss returns the true parameters for every positive penalty weight, and under noise and unmodeled dynamics the parameter error grows at most linearly with the mismatch.
