Signal Processing.summary: Accurate classification of medical time series, such as electrocardiograms (ECGs), requires capturing waveform morphology, long-range temporal structure, inter-lead dependencies, and clinical semantics. Existing large language model (LLM)-based approaches often map signal patches directly into the language embedding space, potentially underusing pretrained time-series knowledge and transferring redundant or irrelevant information. We propose MedTimeQ, a parameter-efficient framework that integrates a lead-aware temporal foundation encoder with an LLM-reprogrammed ECG pathway through gated residual fusion. A Query Former uses learned diagnostic queries to select and compress fused representations into informative soft tokens for a frozen LLM. Semantic prototype learning further guides classification through multiple clinical descriptions per category, statistics-based prompt selection, and knowledge distillation. Both foundation backbones remain frozen, limiting training to lightweight interface and classification components. We evaluate MedTimeQ on PTB-XL, Chapman-Shaoxing, and MIT-BIH for recording-level diagnosis, rhythm classification, and heartbeat classification, respectively. MedTimeQ achieves the best performance in 11 of 12 dataset-metric comparisons, with consistent class-balanced gains across all three tasks. On PTB-XL, it achieves 76.93% accuracy and 58.14% macro-F1, exceeding MedTsLLM by 10.08 and 7.07 percentage points, respectively. These results demonstrate the benefits of selectively integrating pretrained temporal representations with clinical language semantics. Code: https://github.com/kkianamm/MedTimeQ

Signal Processing.title: DIBEM: Diffusion-Based Error Mitigation for Uncertainty-Aware UWB Localization
Signal Processing.summary: Ultra-wideband (UWB) localization degrades substantially under Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) propagation, where multipath and obstruction induce complex ranging error distributions that are poorly represented by fixed parametric models. We propose Diffusion-based Error Mitigation (DIBEM), an uncertainty-aware framework that learns the conditional ranging error distribution directly from six compact Channel Impulse Response (CIR) statistics. Rather than predicting a deterministic correction or restricting uncertainty to a Gaussian or fixed mixture family, DIBEM uses a conditional diffusion model with denoising diffusion implicit model sampling to generate link-specific error samples. The resulting empirical distributions are incorporated into maximum likelihood position estimation. This allows localization to account for heterogeneous ranging uncertainty across anchor-tag links. Experiments across four indoor environments show that DIBEM achieves the lowest negative log-likelihood for NLoS ranging errors and the lowest or tied-lowest mean localization error across all environments. Compared with least squares approaches, DIBEM reduces mean localization error by up to 64.8 percent, while improving over Gaussian and mixture density probabilistic models by up to 15.8 percent and 14.0 percent, respectively. Results demonstrate the potential of diffusion-based conditional error modeling for uncertainty-aware UWB localization, particularly under challenging NLoS propagation.

Signal Processing.title: Approximate Convex Decomposition (ACD) with Divide and Conquer Strategy for DRL-Based BS Localization
Signal Processing.summary: Optimal base station (BS) placement is a fundamental challenge in wireless localization. Conventional optimization approaches may become computationally demanding as the geometric complexity of the environment increases, limiting their scalability to realistic building layouts. This paper proposes an Approximate Convex Decomposition (ACD)-based divide-and-conquer framework integrated with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for optimizing BS placement. The proposed approach exploits the geometric structure of building layouts by partitioning the original environment into smaller sub-regions using cuts associated with reflex vertices. Furthermore, the proposed solution is bench-marked against DRL without ACD and with the optimal solution obtained by exhaustive search. Results show the superiority of the proposed approach and that it approaches the optimal solution.

Signal Processing.title: RF-Florence: Unified RF Detection and Physical Grounding with a Foundation Model
Signal Processing.summary: Reliable signal detection is essential for spectrum sharing and intelligent sensing in sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks. Wideband radio-frequency (RF) monitoring must locate emissions and identify those satisfying waveform-family and physical constraints. The latter task, physical grounding, requires query meaning to agree with measurable signal attributes. RF-Florence unifies three tasks---full-scene detection, physical grounding, and supplied-region recognition---through a shared pretrained foundation model. Calibrated spectrograms connect localization coordinates to time and frequency, while common event targets and explicit predicates align task outputs with requests. On synthetic mixtures with family--attribute combinations withheld from training, structured queries improve mean grounding F1 by 7.66 percentage points over natural language. Under the tested two-path channel, direct grounding with structured queries exceeds a You Only Look Once (YOLO) detector followed by rule-based filtering by 3.44 points in mean F1. These results show the value of aligning query expressions with the signal families and physical variables that define the requested event set.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables

Signal Processing.title: A Closed-Form Soft Spectral Partition for Adaptive Mode Decomposition
Signal Processing.summary: Density-based Adaptive Mode Decomposition (DAMD) shows that the Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) objective, restricted to hard binary partitions, is equivalent to weighted K-means clustering, enabling automatic mode detection. The equivalence concerns detection only; extraction with hard Voronoi masks introduces boundary artefacts. This paper develops a soft extraction theory independent of the detector. First, the hard-partition equivalence is shown to be an algebraic identity that holds if and only if the weights are binary; hard and soft extraction are optima of two different functionals (linear K-means and regularised quadratic VMD) over the same simplex. Second, the regularised soft VMD problem is proved to have a closed-form global optimum, unique on the support of the spectrum: the Lorentzian-weighted partition $s_k^*(ω)\propto[1+2α(ω-ω_k)^2]^{-1}$. Every fixed point of the VMD ADMM mode update is proportional to $|ω-ω_k|^{-2}$; when the dual ascent enforces reconstruction, it is the $α\to\infty$ endpoint of this family. The Lorentzian shape at finite $α$ is therefore a consequence of the regulariser, and $α$ controls how closely the allocation approaches that fixed point. Third, under a Lorentzian spectral prior the partition equals the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) estimator of each mode in the low-noise limit, tying $α$ to the inverse squared mode bandwidth. Since the partition needs only detected centre frequencies, the extraction rule can be switched without recomputing detection. Synthetic experiments with known ground truth test the predictions; four categories of real signals show how much the two allocations differ.
Signal Processing.comment: 27 pages, 9 figures. Accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing. Code: https://github.com/plustar/A-Closed-Form-Soft-Spectral-Partition-for-Adaptive-Mode-Decomposition

Signal Processing.title: Self-Aligned Resonant Beams for Adaptive Beamforming in 6G IoT
Signal Processing.summary: The integration of communication, sensing, and wireless power transfer (WPT) is becoming an important direction for 6G Internet of Things (IoT). However, conventional beamforming typically depends on channel state information (CSI) acquisition, beam training, and active beam scanning, which can introduce substantial overhead in dynamic or passive-device scenarios. This article reviews the radio-frequency resonant beam system (RF-RBS) as a physical-layer self-alignment mechanism for reducing this dependence. By using retro-directive antenna arrays (RAAs) at the transceivers, RF-RBS can form a cyclic electromagnetic feedback loop in which phase-conjugated waves reinforce a dominant round-trip path. This mechanism enables self-aligned, high-gain beam formation under suitable loop-gain, propagation, and hardware conditions. We discuss the RF-RBS architecture, its operating principles, and its potential roles in WPT, self-aligned communication, and passive positioning. We also examine implementation challenges, including analog hardware integration, multi-user interference, limited coverage, and line-of-sight (LoS) dependence, and outline its potential value for latency-sensitive 6G IoT scenarios such as unmanned systems and industrial automation.

Signal Processing.title: On linear MMSE receivers in the presence of data-like multiuser interference
Signal Processing.summary: Linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) receivers have been of great interest for many decades for multi-user interference (MUI) mitigation in radiocommunications networks in particular. Despite the extensive literature on this subject, this topic remains relevant to several current and emerging applications. In this context, the paper presents a continuous-time approach showing that most of LMME receivers of the literature are suboptimal. In particular, they are typically implemented at the symbol rate following matched filtering to the pulse-shaping filter and require a prior knowledge of the MUI channels, which can be difficult and costly to acquire in practice. The main contribution of this paper is to address the key challenge of designing new LMMSE receivers that achieve the performance of the optimal receiver without requiring prior knowledge of the MUI channels. To this end, two novel receiver LMMSE structures are proposed and analyzed for linearly modulated signals impaired by data-like MUI: a two-input receiver and a three-input receiver. The proposed receivers are shown to be quasi-optimal over a broad range of scenarios. These results provide new perspectives for practical implementation of the optimal LMMSE receiver in the presence of data-like MUI, relying only on knowledge of the signal-of-interest (SOI) channel.
Signal Processing.comment: 8 figures

Signal Processing.title: SleepXA: Composing Pretrained Neural and Cardiac Foundation Models for Sleep Representation Learning
Signal Processing.summary: Physiological signals recorded during sleep provide synchronized views of neural, cardiac, respiratory, and other bodily systems, while preserving modality-specific information. Existing EEG and ECG foundation models already capture rich but distinct physiological structure, motivating an alternative to training a multimodal sleep model from scratch: composing existing pretrained models. We introduce SleepXA, a framework that uses synchronized polysomnography (PSG) to compose independently pretrained neural and cardiac foundation models. SleepXA combines pretrained EEG and ECG encoders with lightweight encoders for additional PSG modalities, and learns shared and modality-specific representations through sleep-guided alignment. We pretrain SleepXA on 9,230 overnight PSG recordings from three large cohorts and evaluate it on 27 downstream tasks spanning sleep representation, clinical and disease prediction, and daytime physiological transfer. SleepXA ranks among the top two methods on 22 of 27 tasks. Controlled experiments further show consistent benefits across sensor configurations and EEG-ECG backbone choices, while pretrained initialization outperforms architecture-matched training from scratch and SleepXA surpasses alternative multimodal composition strategies. These results suggest that synchronized multimodal physiology can serve as a natural interface for composing existing physiological foundation models, yielding reusable representations that extend beyond sleep to clinical and daytime physiological settings.
Signal Processing.comment: 36 pages, 16 figures (9 in the main text and 7 in the appendix)

Signal Processing.title: WAFT: A Fourier-Analytic Framework for Steady-State Performance of Walker Constellations
Signal Processing.summary: The Walker configuration is predominantly adopted by nongeostationary orbit constellations exemplified by Starlink and Kuiper. The steady-state distribution of aggregate downlink interference power is critical for spectrum coexistence regulation. Large-scale time-stepped simulation and stochastic geometry (SG)-based models are the mainstream methods for obtaining the distribution, but are either computationally expensive or subject to inherent bias. This paper models the aggregate downlink interference power as an additive observable and proposes the Walker-constellation Analysis via Fourier Transform (WAFT) framework to derive the steady-state performance. Modeling the constellation as a periodic impulse array on the phase torus, the spectral representation of the observable is derived via 2-D Fourier analysis. Analytical expressions for the expectation, variance, and steady-state complementary cumulative distribution function are further derived, and the periodicity of receiver performance along longitude is characterized. For a Starlink sub-constellation example, numerical validation shows that the percentile discrepancies of WAFT relative to a finite-duration time-stepped simulation remain within 0.09~dB. Comparisons with isotropic and intensity-matched SG models reveal that the conditional independence of satellite positions alone makes the models assign a substantial probability mass to physically infeasible values, producing percentile discrepancies.
Signal Processing.comment: 12 pages, 7 figures. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Signal Processing.title: Near-Field Physical-Layer Authentication Under Noisy Enrollment
Signal Processing.summary: In near-field physical-layer authentication (PLA), the receiver estimates a spatial reference from noisy enrollment pilots. With a fixed residual-energy threshold, even a small reference error can cause the false rejection (FR) probability to approach one as the received energy increases. We derive the distribution of the overlap between the true and enrolled spatial directions and use it to calibrate a test based on the aligned energy and the residual-to-aligned energy ratio. The calibration bounds FR for arbitrary regional gains and all legitimate received energies above a prescribed minimum. For a fixed enrolled reference, we reduce the problem of finding the maximum acceptance probability of a multi-antenna attacker to a one-dimensional search. We also derive a pre-enrollment upper bound that holds when the attacker chooses its precoder after observing the enrolled reference. For a single region and a fixed angular threshold, the enrollment energy sufficient to preserve angular separation grows inversely with the square of the available angular margin. In the numerical study with 128 receive elements at 28 GHz, the FR upper bound was 0.9984, including the enrollment outage allowance. At a regional phase perturbation of 20, four regions provided the best trade-off among the tested partitions: its simulated FR was 0.1442, while its false acceptance (FA) at 9 m was 1.084 under the fixed transmit-energy setting.

Signal Processing.title: RadioWorld: Transferring World Models to Radio-Frequency Radiance Fields
Signal Processing.summary: Electromagnetic (EM) wave propagation in the physical world constitutes a Radio-Frequency (RF) radiance field, providing rich information for 6G communication and sensing. However, existing neural RF field methods suffer from three fundamental limitations: (1) they predominantly rely on per-scene optimization and cannot generalize to unseen scenes; (2) they require costly reference RF measurements in each target scene; and (3) they degrade severely when extrapolating beyond the vicinity of reference measurements. To overcome these limitations, we present RadioWorld, a general framework that adapts a world model to synthesize RF radiance fields directly from physical scene geometry and transceiver locations, without requiring any reference RF measurements at inference. Specifically, RadioWorld couples two specialized modules within a dual-stream Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture: a Scene-Understanding Transformer that encodes 3D scene geometry and transceiver locations to extract environment-aware global EM propagation features, and a Field-Generation Transformer that attends to these features to synthesize the RF radiance field with the local query conditions. We also establish UrbanRF-Bench, a large-scale ray-traced benchmark spanning 657 urban scenes and 32,850 RF radiance fields across seven global cities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RadioWorld significantly outperforms specialized baselines and accurately synthesizes RF fields at arbitrary locations in unseen cities. Code, datasets, and checkpoints will be released upon acceptance.

Signal Processing.title: Advanced 400G-SerDes Modulations and Equalizers for GPU Cluster in AI Era
Signal Processing.summary: High-speed GPU cluster interconnects are evolving from 200 to 400 Gbps to meet the growing computing demands of artificial intelligence. We investigate high-order modulation and advanced equalization for 400 Gbps interconnects. Theoretical bit error rate (BER) expressions for 4/8-ary pulse amplitude modulation (PAM) and approximate expressions for six PAM6 formats generated from 32-ary quadrature amplitude modulation (32QAM) are derived. In additive white Gaussian noise, PAM6 generated by framed-cross 32QAM achieves the best BER performance among the PAM6 formats. PAM6 and PAM8 incur peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) penalties of approximately 4.2 and 7.2 dB, respectively, relative to PAM4 at the KP4 forward error correction (KP4-FEC) limit. Simulations compare PAM4, PAM6, and PAM8 at a line rate of 440 Gbps (net rate of 400G) under different bandwidth limitations. As bandwidth becomes more constrained, bandwidth requirements increasingly dominate performance over noise tolerance. PAM4 requires the lowest PSNR to reach the KP4-FEC limit in mildly bandwidth-limited channels, whereas PAM6 performs best under moderate limitations. PAM8 offers a significant advantage under severe limitations because of its lower bandwidth requirement and reduced susceptibility to high-frequency attenuation. With maximum likelihood sequence estimation, PAM6 and PAM8 reach the KP4-FEC limit under all evaluated channel conditions, while PAM6 requires a lower PSNR in most channels, highlighting its potential for 400G-SerDes systems.

Signal Processing.title: Denoised but Not Improved: What EEG Denoising Does to a Downstream Task
Signal Processing.summary: Scalp electroencephalography (EEG) is routinely denoised before it reaches a downstream model, and the denoising literature scores a method by how closely its output matches a clean reference waveform. That reference does not exist for real scalp recordings: it is synthesized by adding artifact templates to signals merely presumed clean, and even an exact separation would return cortical activity blurred by volume conduction rather than the activity itself. Fidelity to it is therefore an unvalidatable objective, and whether it predicts any downstream benefit has gone largely unexamined. We report an audit that examines it. Holding a seizure-detection pipeline fixed and varying only the preprocessing stage, we find that five standard denoising methods, spanning analytic, cross-channel and supervised deep families, all fail to improve on the unprocessed signal, and most degrade it. To say what such a stage must instead do, we formalize a label-only, classifier-free probe that reads it by the separability geometry it induces on task-relevant features, decomposing any change into a between-class distance and a within-class scatter term. On a transform that does improve the task, the probe attributes the entire gain to a roughly one-quarter reduction of within-class scatter, with class separation statistically unchanged. What a downstream model benefits from is therefore variance suppression on task-relevant structure, which waveform-fidelity metrics neither measure nor reward.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted at the IEEE Symposium on CI in Health and Medicine

Signal Processing.title: From Footprints to Service Regions: Modeling and Analysis of Dense LEO Satellite Networks Using an Orbit-Aware Cox Point Process
Signal Processing.summary: In dense low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks, several accessible satellites cover the same location. A footprint therefore identifies where communication is feasible but does not determine which satellite serves each user. The service region of a satellite, namely the set of locations it serves, governs satellite load, resource sharing, and user throughput. Using an orbit-aware Cox point process on a common orbital shell, we model each service region as the intersection of a satellite's spherical-cap footprint and its spherical Voronoi cell under nearest-satellite association. We then use Palm calculus to derive exact expressions for the mean area and perimeter and a coverage--load identity. After coverage saturates, mean area and load decrease inversely with population. In contrast, adding satellites along existing orbits leaves a positive limiting mean perimeter. We connect this geometry to an approximate noise-limited user rate. Along the tested densification paths, the increase in user rate comes mainly from the decrease in mean satellite load rather than from the improvement of the serving link. We also compare the model with Walker constellations with Starlink-type parameters, using Cox parameters matched to the local orbit and satellite densities at each latitude. The model reproduces the mean area and perimeter of these constellations over broad latitude ranges, with larger differences near component maximum latitudes. These results show that service-region geometry, and hence satellite load and user rate, depend not only on the total satellite population but also on its allocation across orbital planes.
Signal Processing.comment: accepted to IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications

Systems and Control.title: Supply Chain Networks: Equilibrium, Sensitivity, Dynamics and Shortage Games
Systems and Control.summary: We model production in a supply chain network in which every node sets a Newsvendor order target, upstream demand is the sum of downstream orders routed through a substochastic matrix, and every node has a capacity. The clearing vector of production quantities is the unique Nash equilibrium of the ordering game and the unique optimal solution of a linear program, and it has the form of the Eisenberg--Noe interbank clearing model. Nodes that produce their order target are hedged; the others are unhedged. We give comparative statics and a closed form for the stationary covariance of node demands. Inventory drawdown after a capacity shock is a Skorokhod reflection problem with a closed-form solution: the network and the unhedged nodes determine who is eventually rationed and by how much, and inventories determine when. When rationed nodes can inflate their orders, the equilibria never lower aggregate deliveries and can make suppliers with no physical shortage unhedged. With endogenous prices, a per-epoch price equilibrium exists and, under mild conditions, is unique when supply is price-elastic. We illustrate the model on global crude-oil trade.
Systems and Control.comment: Working paper

Systems and Control.title: Transferring the driveshaft inertia to the grid via the DC-link in MV drive systems
Systems and Control.summary: This paper investigates a control approach that renders the driveshaft inertia completely available on the grid side and enhances the fault ride-through behavior of medium-voltage (MV) drive systems. Two main contributions are presented. First, we show how the rotational inertia of the driveline shaft can be synchronously coupled to the grid through a modification of the speed control reference signal and through an adapted DC-link control strategy. For the latter, we pursue two alternatives: one based on conventional cascaded control and another based on synchronous machine (SM) model matching. Second, we demonstrate that both the standard phase-locked loop (PLL) and the matching control approach can be interpreted, via the ray-circle complementarity, as feedback optimization schemes with distinct steady-state maps. This perspective allows us to revisit matching control, reveal its embedded PLL, highlight its current-limiting and tracking capabilities, and provide an extensive simulation study.
Systems and Control.comment: Submitted for review to IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology, updated to 22 pages

Systems and Control.title: Global Parameter Identification and Uncertainty Quantification of reduced-order ADM1 using Maximum Likelihood Estimation and Bayesian Inference
Systems and Control.summary: Anaerobic digestion (AD) models can be challenging to calibrate against real data due to limited practical identifiability, data scarcity, and model complexity. Weighted least squares objective functions and gradient-based solvers using finite differences are often used in literature, but result in suboptimal parameter estimates and large uncertainty bands. This paper identifies the parameters of a reduced-order ADM1 by comparing the frameworks of maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) and Bayesian inference (BI), and quantifies uncertainties of parameters and outputs. Multirate experimental data are taken from a lab-scale AD reactor fed with agricultural substrates and operated at organic loading rates of 3$\,$g VS $\mathrm{m^{-3}d^{-1}}$. Global optima are found via global and gradient-based local search algorithms using forward sensitivities. Enhanced scatter search provides the best global search results. These are refined by the Gauss-Newton algorithm as the best local search, which delivers $R^2$ values of 0.95 for acetic acid and 0.77 for biogas production. BI yields substantially narrower uncertainty bands than MLE and avoids the need for a global search by incorporating prior knowledge about parameter distributions. The search space is captured efficiently by log10 scaling of parameters. Algorithmic details on its implications are provided. Despite a high-resolution lab-scale dataset, the ADM1-specific inhibition parameter $K_\mathrm{I,nh3}$ is practically not identifiable with MLE, and shows a low output sensitivity, whereas a parameter for the effective ion concentration shows superb practical identifiabilty at high confidence with both MLE and BI. The present work lays a scalable base for calibration of nonlinear AD models by providing reliable simulations. It thus advances model-based monitoring and control applications of multirate processes such as agricultural AD plants.

Systems and Control.title: Performance Evaluation of Nonlinear Model Predictive and Sliding Mode Controllers on a 4-Cable Spatial CSPR in Simscape
Systems and Control.summary: This paper offers a comprehensive comparative study between Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) and Sliding Mode Control (SMC) applied to a spatial Cable-Suspended Parallel Robot (CSPR) actuated by four cables. The robot is modeled in two parallel ways: (i) via an analytical dynamic model with included cable elasticity and frictional losses, and (ii) in MATLAB Simscape Multibody, capturing realistic physical effects. Both controllers are implemented under identical reference trajectories, system constraints, and tuning strategies. Our results show that NMPC achieves superior tracking accuracy and stronger disturbance rejection compared to SMC, but at the cost of higher computational demand. Moreover, both controllers were tested on an analytical model of the robot and a Simscape model. The close agreement between the two, for both control schemes, confirms the accuracy of the analytical formulation and its consistency with the physics-based simulation. The study highlights the value of physics-based simulation as a complementary tool for validating advanced controllers under realistic conditions, and demonstrates that NMPC offers superior performance for the studied high-precision, constrained CSPR.
Systems and Control.comment: 7 pages, 13 figures, 2 tables. Prepared for the 13th RSI International Conference on Robotics and Mechatronics (ICRoM 2025), Tehran, Iran

Systems and Control.title: Scaled Relative Graph Separation for Unbounded Nonlinear Systems
Systems and Control.summary: We investigate stability analysis of one-channel nonlinear feedback systems based on the recent notion of scaled relative graph (SRG). Our focus is on the SRG separation in the complex plane for feedback stability analysis that involves possibly unbounded open-loop nonlinear systems. Subject to a technical assumption, a homotopy-based SRG separation theorem is developed as the main result, where the incremental directed gap is utilized as a key instrument to quantify robust feedback stability along the homotopy path. Doing so enables us to incorporate commonly used integrators as unbounded systems in the SRG-based framework. Specializations of the main result to linear systems, along with illustrative examples, are also provided to demonstrate its effectiveness.
Systems and Control.comment: An extended version of a conference paper accepted for the 65th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control, 2026

Systems and Control.title: Feed-Forward Dimension Control for High-Dimensional Quantum Key Distribution over Time-Varying Airborne Free-Space Links
Systems and Control.summary: High-dimensional quantum key distribution tolerates more noise than qubit-based protocols, but the dimension that maximizes the secret key depends on turbulence, background light, device imperfections, and block size, all of which change during an airborne or satellite pass. Finite-size security analyses of high-dimensional protocols fix the dimension in advance, and the dimension-adaptive schemes reported so far have been analyzed only asymptotically. Here, a controller sets the dimension, acceptance thresholds, and key length of each block using only public data from earlier blocks. Each block is therefore a standard fixed-length protocol, and composable finite-key security against coherent attacks follows from sequential composition; an inaccurate channel model reduces the key rate but does not weaken security. The controller estimates turbulence from observed error rates, maximizes the expected key under forecast uncertainty, and recalibrates its model online. We evaluate it on a simulated entanglement-based orbital-angular-momentum link between an aircraft and a ground station, using Kolmogorov phase screens and the Hufnagel--Valley turbulence profile. Accounting for forecast uncertainty increases the key by 31\%--47\% relative to a naive planner. Over night, dawn, daytime, and model-mismatch scenarios, the recalibrated controller retains at least 98.8\% of the key obtained with the best fixed dimension for each scenario, while every fixed dimension drops to 73.5\% or less in at least one scenario. Running the link's measurement statistics on a superconducting quantum processor shows device errors close to a constant offset; with these errors included, the best daytime dimension changes from eight to four, and the controller adjusts accordingly.
Systems and Control.comment: 13 pages

Systems and Control.title: Feedback Completion Certificates for Repeated Dwell Tasks with Time Windows
Systems and Control.summary: An inspection robot may owe several measurements at the same station, each with a different window in which a dwell can begin. We ask what a feedback controller must retain about earlier visits to guarantee all remaining deadlines under bounded disturbances. For a common spatial predicate and dwell length, removing redundant windows orders the remaining obligations by both endpoints. On every history without an expired obligation, the served windows form a suffix. One boundary and one capped run length therefore preserve the future satisfaction of the original task. On a verified library of branching motion primitives we use this state to recover a feedback policy. For one task type a scalar threshold per run length suffices, with work linear in the number of listed branches per time layer for fixed dwell. Multiple types require a joint recursion. On a quadrotor inspection library the threshold sweep reduced the cost of constructing a reusable full-domain policy, while a sparse Boolean baseline answered a single initial query faster. In a two-station MuJoCo patrol, three task-aware filters all met every window in twelve paired runs each. Of eight initially certified runs, the completion filter retained the certificate in all eight, compared with three for safety-only filtering.
Systems and Control.comment: 37 pages, including appendices with full proofs and experimental details

Systems and Control.title: Optimal Allocation of Grid-Forming Frequency Shaping Control
Systems and Control.summary: Various inverter-based control strategies have been proposed to improve frequency security for power systems with high renewable penetration. Among them, the grid-forming frequency shaping control is particularly promising due to its ability to shape the post-contingency aggregate system frequency dynamics into first-order with prescribed rate of change of frequency (RoCoF) and steady-state frequency deviation. Moreover, the shaped aggregate dynamics depends on the harmonic sum of all inverter transfer functions rather than on their distribution. In light of this, here we explore how to allocate shaping control resources to minimize the transient control effort needed to achieve ideal coherent dynamics. We formulate it as a constrained optimization problem by tackling two main difficulties. First, we make the squared $\mathcal{H}_2$ norm legitimate quantification of transient control cost under step power imbalances through a system transformation. Second, we simplify the $s$-domain constraint for Nadir elimination into a standard constraint that is easy to implement in optimization. The resulting non-convex optimization problem can be solved by existing successive convexification method. The effectiveness of the allocation has been verified on the modified Icelandic Power Network test case.

Logic in Computer Science.title: Higher Realizability Toposes
Logic in Computer Science.summary: Building on $\infty$-tripos theory, we develop a theory of realizability $\infty$-toposes. We apply $\infty$-tripos theory to construct the function, modified, and Krivine realizability $\infty$-toposes. We recover the Lawvere-Tierney nucleus $j$ that specifies local truth in each construction by exhibiting, for any $n\geq1$, a single family of Eilenberg-MacLane $n$-types whose fibre at an ambient truth value $p$ is contractible after sheafification precisely when $j(p)$ holds. In function realizability, we relate identity types to descriptive set theory. For each $n\geq 2$, we construct a univalent classifier $U_n$ of exact truncation height $n+1$. As maps from Baire space into $U_n$ vary, the sets of inputs admitting a global path from the assigned code to the terminal code are exactly the $G_δ$ subsets of Baire space. After exponentiation by Baire space, the analogous test against the constant map at the terminal code yields exactly the coanalytic sets, at the same truncation height. In modified realizability, a closed proof of local existence under a stable numerical precondition yields a total recursive function together with a coherent proof that its output satisfies the specification whenever the precondition holds. In Krivine realizability, contextual choice for $(n-1)$-truncated families over suitable $n$-types recovers the subterminal defining the Boolean localization. Binary cohomology distinguishes slices of Anel-Awodey-Barton's effective $\infty$-topos even when they share the same ordinary Hyland effective topos and their bases have equivalent spaces of global points. Hyland's effective topos thus occurs as the category of zero-types in infinitely many pairwise inequivalent realizability $\infty$-toposes (recovering Hyland's effective topos as the category of zero-types does not uniquely determine an effective $\infty$-topos).

Logic in Computer Science.title: Higher Duality Theory: Geometric HoTT and Classifying $\infty$-Toposes
Logic in Computer Science.summary: We develop geometric homotopy type theory (geometric HoTT), which gives a dependent language for constructions preserved by inverse images of geometric morphisms. We give a homotopy-coherent calculus for geometric HoTT and extend the classical duality between geometric logic and classifying toposes to Grothendieck $\infty$-toposes. For each geometric type theory, the $\infty$-category of contexts generated by its rules is equivalent to its classifying $\infty$-topos. As the theory varies, the classifier gives a duality of $(\infty,2)$-categories between geometric HoTT theories with interpretations and Grothendieck $\infty$-toposes with geometric morphisms. We then construct a universal family of classifying $\infty$-toposes whose fiber at each presentation of a theory is the classifying $\infty$-topos of that theory. We also construct a universal family of classifying $\infty$-toposes with coherent transport along Morita equivalences of theories. Geometric HoTT thus serves as an internal language for Grothendieck $\infty$-toposes, extending the role of geometric logic in classical topos theory to the realm of $\infty$-topos theory.

Logic in Computer Science.title: TPTL-dist: A Formalised Calculus with Proof Automation for Verifying Real-Time Distributed Systems
Logic in Computer Science.summary: We introduce TPTL-dist, a temporal logic and labelled sequent calculus for specifying and verifying real-time distributed systems. TPTL-dist is formalised in Agda to provide machine-checked correctness and tool support, including automation through a proof search that runs inside Agda. The logic extends Timed Propositional Temporal Logic (TPTL) with past operators, freeze quantification, comparisons between time expressions, domain-specific atoms, and an induction principle on time. We provide a world-based semantics, develop an interval-annotated calculus, and establish its soundness w.r.t. the semantics. To demonstrate its expressiveness, we encode standard distributed system patterns, and we carry out a mechanised proof of a key real-time property of the Pistis Byzantine broadcast protocol. Our results show that TPTL-dist provides a uniform, mechanised framework for reasoning about temporal properties of distributed systems.

Logic in Computer Science.title: Deterministic Proper Positive-Only Learning Is Independent of ZFC
Logic in Computer Science.summary: Binary classification from positive-only samples is a variant of PAC learning in which the learner receives i.i.d. samples only from the positive region of an unknown target concept, but is evaluated on the full distribution. Improper learnability in this model has a textbook characterization, whereas proper learnability has remained open for decades. Recent work characterized it for learners with access to randomness, and showed that, unlike in PAC learning, some classes are properly learnable with randomness but not without it, leaving the deterministic case open. We show that this case cannot be resolved within the standard axioms of mathematics (ZFC): there is a class of VC dimension two whose deterministic proper learnability is independent of ZFC, even though a randomized learner provably learns it. Moreover, no dimension of finite character, a desirable property shared by most dimensions in learning theory, characterizes deterministic proper learnability. We also show that the size of the domain is decisive. In ZFC, deterministic proper learnability has a combinatorial characterization on every domain whose cardinality is below a certain threshold, including every countable domain. In contrast, this characterization fails on every domain of sufficiently large cardinality. Under the generalized continuum hypothesis, this threshold is sharp: it is the exact cardinality at which the characterization starts to fail. Finally, our proofs introduce new tools, based on the Erdos--Rado partition theorem, that may be of broader interest.

Logic in Computer Science.title: Attractors Is All You Need: Parity Games In Polynomial Time
Logic in Computer Science.summary: This paper provides a polynomial-time algorithm for solving parity games that runs in $\mathcal{O}(n^{2}\cdot(n + m))$ time-ending a search that has taken decades. Unlike previous attractor-based algorithms, the presented algorithm only removes regions with a determined winner. The paper introduces a new type of attractor that can guarantee finding the minimal dominion of a parity game. The attractor runs in polynomial time and can peel the graph empty.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: I withdraw this preprint because the algorithm is incorrect. Tom van Dijk provided a four-vertex counterexample, Odd owns all four vertices, labelled by priority. The moves $0\to1\to2\to4$ are forced; from 4, Odd chooses 0 or 2. Even wins every play, yet for d=4 the first pruning step discards the entire Even dominion, contradicting Lemma 3. The claimed polynomial-time result does not follow

Logic in Computer Science.title: Hashing Theorems Modulo Rewrites and Binder Permutation Enables Equivalence Search over 200k Mathlib Theorems
Logic in Computer Science.summary: Like all code, Lean libraries accumulate technical debt and structural deficiencies over the course of their development. A particular concern is duplicate theorems: different parts of a big library can unwittingly contain and prove the same theorem, duplicating maintenance efforts. Tools can help detect redundancy and clean up. For instance, Mathlib's duplicate-declarations linter compares theorem types syntactically after sorting top-level binders and erasing binder information and universe levels. If detecting an equivalence requires unfolding, reorientation, or logical transformations, it escapes this comparison. In this work, we present a method to detect theorems which are equivalent with regard to argument order and currying/uncurrying of dependent types. We implement our method for Lean. By applying it to Mathlib, a library of more than 200k theorems, we demonstrate that it is computationally cheap and scalable. We discuss how our work may enhance efforts to tackle the maintenance burden of Lean libraries.

Logic in Computer Science.title: Complexity as Axiomatic Incompleteness
Logic in Computer Science.summary:
IInformation theory has long sought to uncover the universal laws governing complex systems. Yet information is not merely quantified; it is also interpreted by observers.We formalize this cognitive aspect through a Generalized Incompleteness Theory (GIC), which integrates axiomatic logic, Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) learning, and Gödel's incompleteness theorem to establish a connection between complexity and formal incompleteness. We introduce the notions of interpreter-based information and PAC complexity, demonstrating that certain outputs can be PAC-learnable even when their corresponding interpreters cannot be constructed. We further show that every nontrivial formal system contains a PAC-learnable incompleteness space of dimension \(2^n-n-1\).
  The GIC framework unifies several foundational results-including Cantor's diagonal argument, Gödel's incompleteness theorem, and the Turing halting problem-within a categorical and topological framework. We further show that physical models, including four-dimensional spacetime in relativity and the 11- and 26-dimensional spaces arising in string theory, admit natural correspondences with incompleteness spaces, while critical states can be understood in terms of symmetry-breaking selections of axioms.
  Our framework identifies incompleteness as a universal feature underlying complexity, criticality, and observability, thereby revealing fundamental limits on description and cognition in any axiomatizable theory.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: 70 pages, 15 figures

Logic in Computer Science.title: A detailed verification of Neary's PCP(5) construction
Logic in Computer Science.summary: Neary proved that the Post correspondence problem remains undecidable for instances with five pairs of words. We give a detailed verification of his construction. We first verify the undecidability of the restricted binary tag-system halting problem used in the reduction. We then prove both directions of the reduction to the five-pair problem, using the longer closing pair proposed by Rote. In particular, we show that every solution of the constructed PCP instance yields a halting computation of the simulated tag system.

Logic in Computer Science.title: Fuss-free cumulative universes: theory and practice
Logic in Computer Science.summary: Universes are central to dependent type theory, and they are notoriously difficult to handle in a way that is both correct and usable. We propose a new "fuss-free" generalised algebraic presentation for polymorphic cumulative universes that dispenses with the intricate theory of coherent universe coercions in favour of a simpler formulation, which we prove equivalent by means of a normalisation theorem for the former. We study the fuss-free formulation by means of (1) an abstract specification of its bidirectional elaboration algorithm, and (2) a concrete implementation in Haskell. We also describe and implement an extension of the fuss-free universe hierarchy with a judgemental notion of datatype description from which prior notions of cumulative inductive type may be derived.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: Extended version of a paper to appear in POPL 2027

Logic in Computer Science.title: Probabilistic Timed Automata with Multiple Sure and Threshold Objectives
Logic in Computer Science.summary: Probabilistic timed automata extend the classical timed automata formalism with discrete probabilistic choice over edges. We consider the case of the verification of a combination of multiple objectives of probabilistic timed automata, where the objectives can be non-probabilistic (referring to sure satisfaction of all behaviors) and probabilistic (referring to a probability threshold), and refer to reachability or $ω$-regular properties on executions expressed using parity conditions. We show that existing algorithms for multiple objectives for finite-state Markov decision processes can be applied, using the classical region-graph construction, to obtain algorithms for the corresponding objectives of probabilistic timed automata. In particular, the verification of a probabilistic timed automata against multiple probabilistic-threshold sink-reachability objectives subject to the almost-sure divergence of time is EXPTIME-complete, while verification against the combination of a sure property, including sure divergence of time, and a single probabilistic-threshold parity objective is in NEXPTIME $\cap$ coNEXPTIME.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: 26 pages. Extended version of a paper accepted for publication at SETTA 2026

Logic in Computer Science.title: Two Primes Suffice for Definable Graph Canonisation
Logic in Computer Science.summary: We study inflationary fixed-point logic on finite simple graphs with unordered vertices and an ordered number sort. For a prime $r$, the quantifier $M_r$ tests whether the number of relations satisfying a formula is nonzero modulo $r$. For any distinct primes $p$ and $q$, the logic with $M_p$ and $M_q$ defines the adjacency matrix of a canonical copy on the number sort. On labelled inputs this matrix is computable in deterministic polynomial time with an oracle that tests whether the number of satisfying assignments of a Boolean circuit is nonzero modulo $p$. For each prime $p$, the logic with $M_p$ alone cannot define a canonical copy on all graphs. The primes also differ on Boolean queries. There is a single first-order formula $β(S)$ on vertex sets such that $M_q S β(S)$ is undefinable with $M_p$ alone whenever $p \ne q$. For a positive integer-valued function $g$, consider the class of all graphs $G$ with at most $g(|V(G)|)$ automorphisms. For each fixed prime $p$, the logic with $M_p$ canonises this class exactly when $g$ is bounded.

Logic in Computer Science.title: $\mathsf{Y} \& \mathsf{X}$: Intermediate Logics of Convex Hulls and Cross-Polytopes
Logic in Computer Science.summary: We investigate two logics of geometric Kripke frames: $\mathsf{Y}$, defined by finite convex hulls, and $\mathsf{X}$, defined by cross-polytopes. We characterize the validity of the Kreisel--Putnam axiom on convex hull frames by means of convex independence. Our main technical results concern several reductions obtained using two translations, $C$ and $D$. In particular, we show that $\mathsf{X}$ is invariant under $C$, while $\mathsf{Y}$ is invariant under $D$. Moreover, the same translation $D$ reduces Medvedev logic to every logic in the interval $[\mathsf{Y}',\mathsf{Med}]$, where $\mathsf{Y}'$ is a naturally defined intermediate logic strictly between $\mathsf{Y}$ and $\mathsf{Med}$. Together with geometric arguments, these reductions establish that $\mathsf{Y}$, $\mathsf{X}$, and $\mathsf{Cheq}$ are pairwise incomparable, while each lies strictly between $\mathsf{PL}$ and Medvedev logic. We also prove that every logic in $[\mathsf{Y},\mathsf{Med}]$ is not finitely axiomatizable and that this interval contains continuum many distinct logics. In addition, every logic in $[\mathsf{Y}',\mathsf{Med}]$ is undecidable. We prove that $\mathsf{X}$ is undecidable and $\mathsf{Y}\in Π^0_1$. In particular, we show that it is decidable whether a finite poset is isomorphic to a finite convex hull frame, and that the logics determined by configurations of a bounded number of points are decidable. Finally, we extend our study to infinite convex hull frames. We show that inclusion yields $\mathsf{KC}$, whereas reverse inclusion yields $\mathsf{IPC}$. For the latter result, we use the Cantor set to construct $p$-morphisms onto arbitrary finite rooted frames.

Logic in Computer Science.title: Coalgebra for True Concurrency
Logic in Computer Science.summary: We give the coalgebra for true concurrency along the way paved by traditional coalgebra based on bisimulation. This coalgebra is based on truly concurrent bisimulation, and we give its definition and a simple truly concurrent process algebra.

Logic in Computer Science.title: Containment of Conjunctive Queries with Negative Information over Semirings
Logic in Computer Science.summary: We study the containment problem for (unions of) conjunctive queries ((U)CQs) with negative information on semiring-annotated databases. Our approach to negative information follows the treatment of negation proposed by Grädel and Tannen (2017, 2019, 2021 and 2024) for first-order logic and fixed point logic which applies productively to large classes of semirings, including bounded distributive lattices, as well as the important provenance semirings studied for positive CQ containment by Green (2009). Negation features in (U)CQs along two dimensions: negated equalities (disequations), and negated relational atoms. We study complexity for each of them separately, as well as jointly. For disequations, we extend a methodology that proves the same complexity bounds as the ones already known for the standard Boolean semiring (in the second level of the polynomial hierarchy) for most semirings of interest. Two prominent exceptions are $\mathbb{N}[X]$ and Trio(X) where the complexity bound for containment is in the second level of the counting hierarchy. For CQs with negated relational atoms we show that the complexity, surprisingly, is the same as that of the containment of CQs without negation when one considers model-defining and provenance-tracking interpretations (namely, nondeterministic polynomial time). Interestingly, among bounded distributive lattices, the Boolean two-element case is the only one where the complexity of the problem continues to be hard for the second level of the polynomial hierarchy for model-defining interpretations. Furthermore, we show that the complexity increases again for distributive lattices if we focus on other classes of interpretations. Finally, we consider queries that have both negated equalities and negated relational atoms and show that the complexity of containment continues to be that of the case with just negated equalities.

Logic in Computer Science.title: A logic of strong contingency
Logic in Computer Science.summary: In this paper, inspired by the notions of contingency and strong possibility, we propose a notion which may be called 'strong contingency'. This notion can be seen as a mixture of contingency and strong possibility. We investigate the logic with strong contingency as a sole primitive modality, including its bisimulation notion, expressivity, frame definability, and axiomatizations. It turns out that this logic is expressively incomparable with the standard modal logic and the logic of contingency even over the class of S5-models, and less expressive than the logic of strong possibility and weak necessity over the class of S5-models. Besides, as the introduction of the inequality into the semantics makes the completeness proof much harder, instead of showing the completeness via a canonical model construction, we reduce the soundness and strong completeness of the involved proof systems to those of the existing proof systems in the literature.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: Accepted by the Outstanding Contributions in Logic volume in honor of Lloyd Humberstone

Logic in Computer Science.title: Taming Fitch's and Humberstone's Paradoxes
Logic in Computer Science.summary: Fitch's Paradox says that if every true proposition is knowable, then every true proposition is known. Humberstone's Paradox states that if every true proposition is known by at least one of a set of finitely many agents, then some agent in that set knows every true proposition. Both paradoxes give rise to surprising and unacceptable consequences. In this paper, we diagnose a crucial tacit presupposition underlying these paradoxes, namely that the domain of propositions is closed under Boolean operations such as intersection and union, and offer a uniform resolution. We argue that the paradoxical inferences rely implicitly on this closure assumption. By adopting weak propositionally quantified modal logics that drop these closure conditions, we provide a semantically motivated account that blocks both paradoxes. The restriction on universal instantiation is not an ad hoc technical device, but reflects a conception of propositions as graspable objects of epistemic attitudes, on which the domain of propositions need not be closed under Boolean operations, since some Boolean combinations of graspable propositions may not themselves be graspable.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: Accepted by the Outstanding Contributions in Logic volume in honor of Lloyd Humberstone

Logic in Computer Science.title: Spatial Ensemble Logic for Biomedical Imaging: Geometric Element Ensembles in Euclidean Space
Logic in Computer Science.summary: Ensemble Logic (EL) is a family of modal logics over metric monoids whose modal parameters are terms with quantified variables. We study its member over the Euclidian space, called Spatial Ensemble Logic (SEL), for biomedical images. Geometric element ensembles (GELs) represent atomic propositions by finite lists of effectively presented semi-algebraic sets, principally closed balls. Translation, dilation and erosion preserve individual balls up to emptiness in any dimension. Translation and dilation act element-wise, but element-wise erosion gives only an inner bound. For $k\geq 2$, finite unions of balls are closed under neither intersection nor erosion. We therefore separate record representation from the evaluation domain. Our main result is a satisfaction-preserving translation over GELs into the first-order theory of real closed fields. It yields computable semi-algebraic satisfaction sets, decidable model checking and finite real algebraic evidence. For a fixed formula and dimension, model checking has polynomial data complexity under stated rationality and bounded-degree assumptions. Combined complexity is PSPACE-hard and in EXPSPACE. On the line, rational interval data admit linear-arithmetic evaluation with rational evidence, under rationality assumptions on the norm, query and evaluation point. For $k\geq 2$, rational balls can force irrational witnesses. Lower and upper annotation bounds propagate through formulas. Synthesis of a ball ensemble is decidable within a prescribed budget of balls and undecidable without one. In a vascular use case, medial ball ensembles decide calibre and stenosis queries at stored centers by comparing stored numbers. We also examine how far evaluation can proceed element-wise when the union forming a support is deferred to the point of evaluation.

Signal Processing.title: FAS-Assisted Self-Interference Mitigation for In-Band Full-Duplex Communications
Signal Processing.summary: In-band full-duplex (IBFD) communication relies on effective self-interference cancellation (SIC) to overcome the strong loopback self-interference (SI). While fluid antenna system (FAS)-assisted SIC offers superior SI suppression by dynamically selecting the FAS port to minimize the residual SI power, it incurs high pilot overhead to acquire channel state information (CSI) for both forward and loopback channels. This raises the question of whether forward channel CSI is necessary for effective SI mitigation. To address this challenge, we propose a pilot-efficient FAS-assisted SI mitigation (FAS-SIM) approach that selects the FAS port solely based on the loopback SI channel. Theoretical performance analysis of the forward signal is provided. Numerical results then reveal that FAS-SIM achieves SI suppression and a forward-link rate comparable to the conventional method, while reducing port-selection training overhead by 50%, offering a low-overhead solution for IBFD communications.

Signal Processing.title: StreamingDPD: A 1.28-GSa/s Instantaneous-Power-Gated Depthwise TCN Accelerator for Real-Time 320-MHz Digital Predistortion
Signal Processing.summary: State feedback between successive samples limits the streaming throughput of recurrent neural networks for digital predistortion (DPD). We present StreamingDPD, an accelerator that processes 320-MHz signals at 1.28 GSa/s. Its 207-parameter instantaneous-power-gated depthwise temporal convolutional network (IPG-DWTCN) uses $|x[n]|^2$ to gate feature channels and causal dilated depthwise convolutions to model power amplifier memory. The network maps to a spatially unrolled fixed-point pipeline with shift-based quadratic activations and layer-wise mixed precision, sustaining one complex sample per cycle per lane. Its algorithmic cost is 554 floating-point operations per complex sample, 30.1% fewer than the recurrent baseline with the best linearization performance. In RF playback measurements on three power amplifiers driven by 40- to 320-MHz Wi-Fi 6/7 and 5G NR waveforms, IPG-DWTCN achieves the lowest mean adjacent-channel power ratio (ACPR) and ranks first or ties for first in mean error vector magnitude (EVM) against five neural baselines of comparable size. Four-lane FPGA hardware-in-the-loop tests on a 320-MHz 4096-QAM Wi-Fi 7 waveform achieve -45.82 dBc ACPR and -42.94 dB EVM at 1.28 GSa/s. At the same sample rate, post-layout evaluation of a single-lane 12-nm FinFET ASIC yields a 0.10 mm$^2$ core, a 52-cycle (40.63 ns) latency, and an estimated typical-corner power of 142.21 mW (111.10 pJ/sample). Relative to the prior 22-nm recurrent DPD ASIC, the design provides 5.1 times the throughput at about one-seventh the energy per sample.

Signal Processing.title: TrustFlow-ECG: Reliability-Aware ECG Restoration with Calibrated Risk Estimation
Signal Processing.summary: Electrocardiogram (ECG) restoration models can reduce noise and motion artifacts, but they rarely estimate whether the restored waveform is reliable for downstream analysis. We propose TrustFlow-ECG, a reliability-aware restoration framework that combines a one-step conditional rectified-flow restorer with a lightweight window-level risk predictor. The predictor uses the noisy ECG, restored ECG, and correction residual, then applies validation-set isotonic calibration for selective ECG analysis. We evaluate on MIT-BIH ECG windows corrupted with NSTDB artifacts, powerline interference, and mixed noise across multiple SNRs, with an external 9,675-window PTB-XL stress check without retraining. TrustFlow achieves 0.862 Spearman correlation with true risk and 0.911 AUROC for failure detection, while calibration reduces ECE from 0.0385 to 0.0098. At 80% coverage, selective rejection reduces RMSE from 0.1848 to 0.1345, improves R-peak F1 from 0.8778 to 0.9175, and reduces HR MAE from 6.26 to 4.88 bpm.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages. Preprint. Under review

Signal Processing.title: Multi-Sensor Fusion for False-Alarm Reduction by Timed Electromechanical Corroboration
Signal Processing.summary: A physician checks the clinical electrocardiogram against other observations. A wearable monitor has no physician. This paper shows that a mechanical sensor worn beside the electrocardiogram can take over that check, and that the right added sensors lower false alarms further. A beat is accepted only when a mechanical contraction follows at the delay learned for the wearer. Beat-shaped artifacts injected into resting and exercise recordings passed the electrocardiogram alone almost every time. A seismocardiogram or phonocardiogram as the second channel rejected most while keeping nearly all true beats, strongly at rest and partly during exercise. Shifting the mechanical signal in time removed the benefit. A detection criterion scores an added sensor by the part of its response that the sensors in place cannot predict. With four sensors, this score ranked the sets as their measured false-alarm rates did. With the two sensors it selected, 6.2 percent of the artifacts passed while 95 percent of true beats were kept, half the rate of the best single sensor. In integer arithmetic on a low-cost microcontroller, the detector made the same decisions as the software. These rates come from injected artifacts, not alarms in patients. Natural motion and clinical events remain untested.
Signal Processing.comment: 8 pages, 8 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics

Signal Processing.title: Structured Adaptive Tensor Prediction for Streaming Data
Signal Processing.summary: Matrix-valued time series arise in a wide range of applications, such as spatio-temporal data in medical imaging and geophysics. Existing forecasting methods are mainly designed for static settings, while adaptive filtering techniques have been largely limited to scalar- or vector-valued data. In this paper, we develop an adaptive tensor prediction framework for streaming matrix-valued data based on a Tensor-on-Matrix (ToM) regression model, in which the responses in a sliding window are lifted to a third-order tensor and the regression tensor is updated online by stochastic gradient descent (SGD). We derive the leading terms of the steady-state and tracking errors of SGD with overlapping windows, which show that the steady-state error is proportional to the step size and the noise variance, and that the step size governs a trade-off between noise and tracking. We further analyze the statistical accuracy of structured ToM regression within a single window. We establish a restricted isometry property, which holds when the window length is proportional to the input dimension, and derive recovery error bounds for sparse, low-rank and sparse plus low-rank regression tensors, which show that the recovery error scales with the intrinsic degrees of freedom rather than the ambient dimension. Simulations confirm the theoretical results, and the effectiveness of the structured adaptive updates is validated on the tracking of a drifting quantum gate, citywide crowd-flow prediction, and global total electron content (TEC) forecasting.

Signal Processing.title: Merits of Collocating Uptilted Antennas on Terrestrial Base Stations for Aerial Coverage
Signal Processing.summary: The integration of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) into future wireless networks introduces challenges in ensuring reliable aerial coverage, particularly for UAV-based user equipment (UAV-UE). Traditional terrestrial base stations (BSs) with downtilted antennas, referred to as dt-BSs, are designed primarily for ground users. They provide inefficient connectivity to UAV-UE due to weak sidelobe gains, and susceptibility to ground reflection (GR) interference as well as sidelobe interference from non-serving dt-BSs. To address this, we propose a hybrid cellular architecture that collocates uptilted antennas on a portion of existing dt-BS towers, referred to as ut-BSs. These support UAV-UE exclusively, minimizing impact on ground users. We consider realistic antenna radiation patterns and probabilistic line-of-sight (LoS)/non-LoS (NLoS) links between ut-BSs and UAV-UE. Using stochastic geometry, we analyze the UAV-UE coverage probability, accounting for interference from both dt-BSs and non-serving ut-BSs, along with GR-induced interference. Results show significant improvements in UAV-UE coverage with only a small density of ut-BSs. GR interference is notable at lower altitudes but diminishes beyond 500 meters. This study highlights the potential of our hybrid architecture to enhance the reliability and scalability of UAV communications in large-scale deployments. It also offers actionable insights for telecom operators considering the collocation of uptilted antennas within existing infrastructure to better support aerial connectivity.

Signal Processing.title: Twisted Block Particle Filters: A Local Particle-System Change of Measure for High-Dimensional State-Space Models
Signal Processing.summary: Block particle filters mitigate weight degeneracy in high-dimensional state-space models, but their normalizer estimates can remain highly variable. We introduce a twisted block particle filter (TBPF) that incorporates predictive guidance through an exact change of measure at blockwise resampling. The method guide-tilts one uniformly selected offspring per block, leaves the state-transition kernel unchanged, and computes the resampling correction using finite empirical guide averages. We prove that this correction exactly preserves the finite-particle block particle filter normalizer expectation, separating the effect of guided sampling from the approximation introduced by spatial blocking. Our analysis provides exact conditional local moments and a one-step conditional central limit result. We further derive explicit bounds on the correction accumulated across blocks and time, establish fixed-horizon consistency of the block filter and corrected normalizer under suitable regularity and guide-range conditions, and identify conditional criteria for guide perturbations that reduce variance. Experiments on coupled linear Gaussian and stochastic-volatility models with up to 256 latent dimensions show lower measured log-normalizer variance. For stochastic volatility with a five-step guide, the median reduction is $38\%$. An application to a 100-dimensional financial portfolio panel extends the evaluation to real data.
Signal Processing.comment: 44 pages

Signal Processing.title: Winning Solution to UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge 2026 (V2X-Real Track): Site-Calibrated Synthetic Data and Multi-Detector Fusion
Signal Processing.summary: This work summarizes a winning solution for the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge (V2X-Real track) at the IEEE BigData Cup 2026. The primary objective is to train 3D detectors for vehicles, pedestrians, and trucks using only synthetic roadside LiDAR data, and to generate synthetic scans that are sufficiently realistic to be indistinguishable from real ones. A CARLA-based pipeline was developed and calibrated to the fixed sensor site, accurately modeling the range image, including no-return beams, based on unlabeled real development scans. A combined inference detector, utilizing multiple 3D detectors (VoxelNeXt, PV-RCNN, and SECOND) trained exclusively on synthetic data, was also proposed. Each scan was aligned to the synthetic ground plane and processed through the detectors at multiple ground heights. The resulting bounding boxes were fused using bird's-eye view (BEV) clustering, followed by class-specific post-processing to refine heading and box size and to filter low-confidence detections. The final submission tied for first place with a combined score of 0.8947. The ablation study demonstrated that per-scan ground leveling more than doubled the real-scan mAP, while fusing boxes across different heights and models further improved performance. The proposed work narrows the gap between synthetic and real LiDAR data for 3D object detection in urban V2X scenarios. Reproducible code is available at https://github.com/Arnavvvkumar/IEEE-BigData-2026-Cup---V2X-Track

Signal Processing.title: Adaptive Filtering With Reduced Computational Complexity Using SOPOT Arithmetic
Signal Processing.summary: Implementing finite impulse response (FIR) adaptive filters by employing the sums of signed-powers-of-two (SOPOT) arithmetic may lead to simpler hardware and consequently reduced power consumption. In this paper, one evaluates the effects of SOPOT arithmetic on the adaptive filter's recursion algorithms. The filters' coefficients and algorithms' underlying variables are fully operated using SOPOT arithmetic in the whole iterative process. More specifically, one evaluates convergence rate, numerical stability, and accuracy since using few signed-powers-of-two (SPT) terms propagates numerical errors during the adaptive cycle that may impair the algorithm behavior. The SOPOT approximations are obtained through the technique known as Matching Pursuits with Generalized Bit-Plane (MPGBP) algorithm, with notable cost-performance trade-off and low computational complexity. Results are provided for the Least-Mean-Squares (LMS), the Normalized Least-Mean-Squares (NLMS) and the Recursive-Least-Squares (RLS) algorithms, considering adaptive filters employed for system identification and change detection.

Signal Processing.title: A General Non-Stationary Channel Model for Autonomous Vehicle Communications in Underground Spaces
Signal Processing.summary: Autonomous vehicles exhibit high mobility and environmental adaptability, making them well-suited for underground inspection and rescue missions. In this paper, a general three-dimensional (3D) non-stationary geometry-based stochastic model (GBSM) is proposed for autonomous vehicle communications in underground spaces. The proposed channel model accounts for the 3D mobility of autonomous vehicles and can be adapted to pillar, tunnel, and cave scenarios. To characterize the structural and physical features of underground spaces, the proposed model incorporates the generation and evolution of spatially dispersed and/or directionally confined clusters along with their constituent specular/dense multipath components (SMCs/DMCs). Additionally, the proposed channel model considers channel non-stationarity, waveguide effect, and near-field/far-field effects. Statistical properties, including space-time-frequency correlation functions (STF-CFs), delay/angular/Doppler power spectral densities (PSDs), root mean square (RMS) delay spread, and stationary interval, are derived and analyzed. The validity of the proposed channel model is substantiated through comparative analysis between measurement and simulation results.

Signal Processing.title: Beyond Raw IQ: Compact Semantic Representations for Task Oriented Automatic Modulation Classification
Signal Processing.summary: Automatic modulation classification (AMC) is an important component of modern wireless communication systems, but conventional signal representations can be expensive to store, process, and communicate, particularly under noisy channel conditions. This work investigates whether learned semantic representations can provide a compact alternative to high-dimensional in-phase and quadrature (IQ) representations while retaining robustness to noise. Starting from a 2048-dimensional IQ representation, we evaluate learned semantic representations with dimensions of 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64. Across the evaluated configurations, a 16-dimensional representation provides the strongest overall trade-off between classification performance, robustness, and representation size. The resulting representation achieves a 128x compression ratio and a 99.22% reduction in dimensionality. We further evaluate representation stability across signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), compare semantic representations with a raw-IQ CNN, analyze per-class robustness, and perform five-seed validation. The five-seed evaluation produces an average accuracy of (49.22 +- 0.52)% and Macro-F1 of (49.27 +- 0.53)% across the evaluated SNR range. These results indicate that learned semantic compression can produce a substan- tially smaller representation while preserving useful classification information and improving geometric stability under noise.
Signal Processing.comment: 14 pages

Signal Processing.title: R2WM: Recursive Reasoning Wireless Model for Long-Horizon mmWave Beam Prediction
Signal Processing.summary: Long-horizon beam prediction aims to extend beam-training intervals while supporting beam alignment in mobile millimeter-wave systems. Although pretrained large models can improve prediction over compact recurrent baselines, their large backbones impose substantial storage and computing requirements. To address this limitation, we propose a recursive reasoning wireless model (R2WM). Given a fixed history of beam indices and angles of departure (AoDs), R2WM repeatedly updates coupled latent and prediction states using a shared causal-attention backbone before jointly decoding the future beam indices. Backbone reuse increases computational depth at fixed parameter count. In the standard 10-step DeepMIMO setting, R2WM achieves an average normalized beamforming gain of 0.9597, compared with 0.8629 for the prompt-as-prefix large language model, with 99.1% fewer parameters and 59.1% fewer counted floating-point operations. Transfer experiments show that R2WM retains normalized gain under the tested carrier-frequency and antenna-count changes, while its beam-index-only variant retains gain under the tested base-station change. Component ablations show higher gains with historical AoD conditioning and causal attention. Recursion analysis reveals a gain-computation trade-off across separately trained configurations with the same parameter count. An additional comparison with a nonrecursive Transformer of similar parameter count shows higher gain for R2WM at greater computational cost. These results support accurate long-horizon beam prediction without a large pretrained backbone.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 8 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication as a Correspondence in IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology

Signal Processing.title: Operating-Condition Normalization in C-MAPSS: Matched Historical Baselines, Multi-Seed Robustness, and Prognostic-Score Trade-offs
Signal Processing.summary: Operating-state changes can obscure turbofan degradation signals, but a reduction in remaining-useful-life (RUL) error after condition-wise standardization may reflect weaknesses of the comparison features instead of a unique benefit of normalization. A controlled retrospective audit examines NASA C-MAPSS FD002 and FD004 with engine-disjoint folds, raw condition identifiers, two constructions of causal history, early-life baselines, and continuous operating-setting correction. Ridge regression, random forests and XGBoost are compared under explicit training-engine-only fitting rules. The previously reported XGBoost FD004 terminal RMSE decreased from 30.38 to 29.08 cycles following six-condition standardization; however, raw sensor values accompanied by condition-matched histories and condition identifiers achieved 28.09 cycles, reversing the naive point estimate ranking, although the paired-engine interval spans zero. For FD002, normalized XGBoost reduced terminal RMSE yet increased the asymmetric NASA score (12,616 to 13,289). Additional model-seed, condition count, RUL-cap, grouped-validation and explanation checks test sensitivity rather than postulating a universally optimal representation. The six clusters reproduce known simulator operating regimes; no new condition discovery algorithm, causal diagnostic method, or field ready prognostic system is claimed. Since the official test endpoints were also used in earlier exploratory comparisons, all newly examined alternatives are reported as retrospective benchmark evidence, not as results from a pristine confirmatory holdout.

Signal Processing.title: VEGA: A Scalable Software-Hardware Co-design for Genome Alignment using RVV Extension
Signal Processing.summary: Dynamic programming (DP)-based genome sequence analysis is fundamental to computational genomics, but it remains computationally intensive as genomic data volumes continue to outpace Moore's Law. Existing hardware accelerators often sacrifice programmability and scalability across diverse alignment algorithms. In this work, we present VEGA, a scalable software-hardware co-design that accelerates genome alignment using RISC-V Vector extensions. VEGA introduces specialized vector instructions and three key innovations: a Forefront Stationary dataflow that minimizes off-chip memory access, intersequence parallelism that maximizes SIMD lane utilization, and custom ISA extensions that accelerate core alignment operations. Evaluations show that VEGA achieves up to 15.1x and 9.7x speedups for Edit Distance and Smith-Waterman algorithms over the Ara2-RVV vector baseline, sustaining 10.2x and 6.7x gains for 10kbp sequences. Post-synthesis results indicate only 1.0% area overhead compared to a standard RISC-V core, with performance-per-area efficiency rivaling specialized ASICs. VEGA thus achieves a balanced advancement in efficiency, programmability, and scalability for genome sequence alignment.

Signal Processing.title: Non-Square UPA-Enabled XL-MIMO Systems: Anisotropic Near-Field Characterization, Fundamental Limits, and Channel Estimation
Signal Processing.summary: Extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) is crucial for next-generation communication systems.
